🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of land required for railway projects: Ashwini Vaishnav

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:04:58 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Stating that the Tamil Nadu government will have to do its duty of acquiring land if all sanctioned railway projects are to be implemented in the State, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the total land acquired so far stood at only 24% of the land required.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Speaking at a Constitution Day event organised by the State BJP unit in the city on Thursday, Mr. Vaishnav said, that out of a total requirment of 4,800 hectares of land, the State has managed to acquire only 1,253 hectares. “My request to the TVK is, please take this as a challenge. Acquire the land [and] we will [carry out] each and every project without any hassle...don’t shy away from your responsibilities,” he emphasised. Projects sanctioned for development of railways in Tamil Nadu amounted to Rs. 48,000 crore, he added. Taking a dig at the State government over the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, Mr. Vaishnav said, “You can stop one deepam to be lighted, but you cannot stop the Tamil people from progress. Stopping one deepam, you have disturbed the emotions of millions of people.” Listing out some of the projects undertaken, the minister said that 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu are being reconstructed. Construction was underway in stations like Chennai Egmore, Madurai, and Katpadi, while construction work has been completed in Chinna Salem, Morappur, Manapparai, Pollachi, Thiruvarur, Coonoor, and Udhagamandalam. Nine Vande Bharat services are being operated in Tamil Nadu, he maintained. Bullet trains, once introduced, will cut the journey from Chennai to Bengaluru to merely 73 minutes. Also, the Hyderabad-Amaravati-Chennai distance will take three hours to complete, the minister added. He added that in Gummidipoondi, the Ramkrishna Titagarh Rail Wheels Ltd’s forged wheel factory was ready and would soon roll out high strength railway wheels which will be exported to Europe as well. Earlier, BJP State President Nainar Nagendran put forth a series of requests, including installing a statue of former chief minister M.G. Ramachandran at the Chennai Central Railway Station, reopening of Kallur station near Tirunelveli, introducing sleeper coaches in Vande Bharat trains, and a stop at Thalaiyuthu station for trains running between Coimbatore and Tirunelveli. The minister immediately got on his phone passing the demands on to railway officials and setting a timeline for the same, which drew applause from the crowd.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamilisai Soundararajan, senior BJP leader, requested the minister to install a statue of freedom fighter Vanchinathan at the Vanchi Maniyachchi Junction in Thoothukudi district.

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Construction (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Construction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation. During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese. Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion. Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history. The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027. When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State. As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.”
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:01:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation. During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese. Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion. Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history. The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027. When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State. As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

स्वतंत्रता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Independence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Experts examine key aspects, challenges of condu' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Experts examine key aspects, challenges of co' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Experts examine key aspects, challenges of co' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C." (Hinglish Arth: सेवानिवृत्त आईएएस अधिकारी सी के बीच एक आकर्षक बातचीत।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा कि आधुनिक तकनीक के साथ यह अभ्यास अधिक कुशल और तेज हो सकता है।)

articles.title: Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27 seeking a personal affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary detailing the government’s decision-making, including any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court. The petition filed by Rama Ravikumar was orally mentioned before a Bench headed by Justice Arvind Kumar at 2 p.m. The petition, settled by senior advocate P. Valliappan and filed by advocate G. Balaji, also sought the immediate preservation and production of all physical and electronic records relating to the implementation of the November 20 order. It has made both Tamil Nadu authorities and the temple administration parties in the contempt case. Other documents sought to include the November 23 prohibitory order and the resolution of the Board of Trustees, including the opinions purportedly obtained from the Agama experts and Sthanikars. The petition said the court must initiate suo motu criminal contempt proceedings. The plea also urged the apex court to invoke its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution for lighting the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon in Thirupparankundram Hill on a substituted date within seven days, preferably during the current Tamil month of Karthigai, subject to the safeguards prescribed in the November 20 order, and under the personal supervision of the State Chief Secretary, with the assistance of an independent Court Commissioner and the Central Reserve Police Force. In the morning, Justice Kumar verbally conveyed that an application to shift the Karthigai Deepam flame from the Deepa Mandapam to the Deepathoon and contempt petitions filed against State authorities for failing to comply with the November 20 order to light the sacred lamp on the stone pillar would be listed on November 27. In one of these contempt petitions, Hindu Dharma Parishad has sought the initiation of action against T.G. Vinay, Commissioner, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Department; Nishant Krishna, District Collector, Madurai; and S. Rajendiran, Madurai Commissioner of Police. The Hindu parties are seeking contempt action despite Mr. Krishna’s preliminary report of November 25, which stated that the district authorities had made all arrangements to facilitate the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon in compliance with the November 20 order. However, the Board of Trustees at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple had not authorised persons for the lamp-lighting team on November 24. Another contempt plea, drawn by advocate Yashika Anand and filed through advocate Narender Kumar Verma, said the non-compliance with the apex court order of November 20 to light the lamp on November 24 at the Deepathoon as a “limited one-time arrangement” only for this year was not only contumacious but also a patent violation of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution. “It amounts to invasion of legitimate expectation duly sanctioned by the Supreme Court,” the petition said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karthigai deepam lit only at traditional spot atop Thirupparankundram hills

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Thirupparankundram ‘deepathoon’ row: Supreme Court agrees to list plea to detail Vijay’s role

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 12:58:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) allowed the listing of a contempt petition on November 27 seeking a personal affidavit from the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary detailing the government’s decision-making, including any role played by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon on the Thirupparankundram Hill summit in compliance with the November 20 order of the court. The petition filed by Rama Ravikumar was orally mentioned before a Bench headed by Justice Arvind Kumar at 2 p.m. The petition, settled by senior advocate P. Valliappan and filed by advocate G. Balaji, also sought the immediate preservation and production of all physical and electronic records relating to the implementation of the November 20 order. It has made both Tamil Nadu authorities and the temple administration parties in the contempt case. Other documents sought to include the November 23 prohibitory order and the resolution of the Board of Trustees, including the opinions purportedly obtained from the Agama experts and Sthanikars. The petition said the court must initiate suo motu criminal contempt proceedings. The plea also urged the apex court to invoke its plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution for lighting the ceremonial lamp at Deepathoon in Thirupparankundram Hill on a substituted date within seven days, preferably during the current Tamil month of Karthigai, subject to the safeguards prescribed in the November 20 order, and under the personal supervision of the State Chief Secretary, with the assistance of an independent Court Commissioner and the Central Reserve Police Force. articles.title: Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 12:48:13 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked at how youth hostels and tourism can promote physical and mental well-being.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India was represented by Haritha Nagaveni Naganaboina of Visakhapatnam and Mithil Manoj Joshi of Goa. Ms. Haritha spoke on the country’s experience of youth health and well-being. Organised by Qatar Youth Hostels in partnership with UNICEF, the forum focused on United Nations Sustainable Development Goal, SDG-3: Good Health and Well-being. The theme was chosen by participants through a vote at the end of the previous edition. The forum aims to develop youth-led recommendations and programmes that link health and well-being with sustainable tourism, in line with the Qatar National Youth Policy. The participating countries were Qatar, the host, Bahrain, Libya, Lebanon, Slovenia, India, Pakistan and Spain. Ms. Haritha, 28, said the two of them were the only participants from India. Mr. Joshi is 25. The programme combined interactive sessions and workshops meant to build partnerships among youth hostel representatives. UNICEF and Qatari ministry representatives opened the ceremony, and addressed the delegates, she said. Participants attended eight workshops over two days. In one, groups were asked how tourism and wellness could be combined in Qatar. Ms. Haritha led her group in pitching “Blue Steps”, a beach walk proposal that the session host liked. Each country also made a presentation, and hers was on India’s experience. Extreme heat keeps most people in Qatar indoors, Ms. Haritha said, with residents travelling largely by car or metro. She was told that parks and cycling facilities were being developed there, and felt the idea could work in Visakhapatnam, which has a coastal setting and is not as hot. Delegates from other countries, she found, shared similar concerns, among them the need for a digital detox, and drew on their own geography for activities such as mountaineering and kayaking. Ms. Haritha, who holds an LL.M. from Middlesex University, London, and an LL.B. from Andhra University, is a former junior advocate. She has been associated with the Youth Hostels Association of India for about 13 years. The Andhra Pradesh branch recommended her to the national office, and she credits its chairman, Ch. Ravi Paul, for urging her to apply.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.

सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Presentation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Presentation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ bea' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ bea' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Young people from eight countries met in Doha from November 8 to 11 for the fourth edition of the Youth at Hostel, International Forum, which looked..." (Hinglish Arth: यूथ एट हॉस्टल, इंटरनेशनल फोरम के चौथे संस्करण के लिए आठ देशों के युवा 8 से 11 नवंबर तक दोहा में मिले, जिसमें इस बात पर विचार किया गया कि युवा हॉस्टल और पर्यटन शारीरिक और मानसिक कल्याण को कैसे बढ़ावा दे सकते हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Vizag youth advocate pitches ‘Blue Steps’ beach walk at Doha wellness forum"?

B. Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Back home, she hopes to organise a five-day trek through forest to the Katiki waterfalls in Araku, and will propose it to the State branch." articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days. The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” . “To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said. Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:34:56 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill. The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13. Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days. The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001. Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day. Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” . “To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said. Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions. Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Communication (Noun)
संचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Communication' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Delimitation (Adjective / Verb)
हदबंदी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Delimitation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Proportional (Adjective)
आनुपातिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Proportional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government..." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight." (Hinglish Arth: इस उभरती स्थिति में, सभी की निगाहें 22 लोकसभा सांसदों वाली डीएमके और आठ सांसदों वाली एनसीपी (शरदचंद्र पवार) पर हैं।)

articles.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098. Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help! Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer. With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — नवीनतम राष्ट्रीय परिवार स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण (2023-24) के अनुसार, बाल विवाह के सबसे अधिक प्रसार वाले भारत के राज्यों में राजस्थान छठे स्थान पर है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — गरीबी, शिक्षा की कमी और असंतुलित लिंग अनुपात के कारण मजबूत आटा-सट्टा जैसी प्रथाएं, विशेष रूप से आदिवासी और ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में इस प्रथा को बढ़ावा दे रही हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — अशोक कुमार की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, अब शिक्षा और सोशल मीडिया तक अधिक पहुंच से सशक्त लड़कियों की बढ़ती संख्या ना कह रही है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

hinglishTracks.en: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — राजस्थान के सीकर में रहने वाली 16 साल की नंदिनी (बदला हुआ नाम) ने अपना भविष्य तय कर लिया था: स्कूल खत्म करो, कॉलेज जाओ और आर्थिक रूप से स्वतंत्र होने के लिए नौकरी करो।।

hinglishTracks.en: Her family, however, had other plans.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालाँकि, उसके परिवार की अन्य योजनाएँ थीं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent.

hinglishTracks.en: Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — अगले कुछ दिनों में, नंदिनी ने छह से अधिक बार हेल्पलाइन पर कॉल किया, उसके हाथ में जो भी फोन आया, उसका इस्तेमाल किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — कभी-कभी, वह दिखावा करती थी कि वह अपने भावी दूल्हे से बात करना चाहती थी; अन्य समय में, वह अपने दोस्तों से संपर्क करने की कोशिश करती थी।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Prospective' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: भावी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prospective' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — लेकिन प्रत्येक कॉल में एक जरूरी संदेश था: शादी की तैयारी चल रही थी, मेहमानों को आमंत्रित किया जा रहा था, और तारीख करीब आ रही थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — हर बार कॉल जिला बाल संरक्षण कार्यालय से कनेक्ट हो रही थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: “She had asked us not to contact her.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — “उसने हमसे उससे संपर्क न करने के लिए कहा था।।

hinglishTracks.en: She said she would call whenever she got a chance.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — उन्होंने कहा कि जब भी मौका मिलेगा वह फोन करेंगी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उनकी पहली कॉल शादी से ठीक तीन दिन पहले आई थी,'' जिला बाल संरक्षण अधिकारी गार्गी शर्मा याद करती हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — बमुश्किल 72 घंटे की कार्रवाई में, टीम ने अदालत से निषेधाज्ञा प्राप्त कर ली और शादी रोक दी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — जब अधिकारी पहुंचे तो परिवार आश्चर्यचकित रह गया, उन्हें संदेह हुआ कि किसी पड़ोसी ने उन्हें सूचित किया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने कभी सोचा भी नहीं था कि उनके बीच की शांत स्कूली छात्रा अपने बचाव की योजना बना रही थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — मुखबिर के रूप में उसकी पहचान गुप्त बनी रही।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — सीकर प्रशासन ने 2024 में 29 और 2025 में 10 बाल विवाह रोके।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — शर्मा कहते हैं, ''2026 में हमें अब तक 21 मामलों की जानकारी मिली है.''।

hinglishTracks.en: But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — लेकिन कई नंदिनी हैं, खासकर भारत के गांवों में, जिनके पास बाल विवाह को न कहने की शिक्षा या एजेंसी नहीं है।।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:45:13 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098. Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help! Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer. With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Elimination (Noun)
उन्मूलन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Elimination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Prospective (Adjective)
भावी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prospective' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spok' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spok' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey..." (Hinglish Arth: नवीनतम राष्ट्रीय परिवार स्वास्थ्य सर्वेक्षण (2023-24) के अनुसार, बाल विवाह के सबसे अधिक प्रसार वाले भारत के राज्यों में राजस्थान छठे स्थान पर है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage." (Hinglish Arth: लेकिन कई नंदिनी हैं, खासकर भारत के गांवों में, जिनके पास बाल विवाह को न कहने की शिक्षा या एजेंसी नहीं है।)

• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

articles.title: BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year. The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA. On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun. “This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday. Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said. There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / government

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:23:07 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year. The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA. On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun. “This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday. Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said. There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India / government

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Verification (Noun)
सत्यापन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Verification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Residential (Adjective)
आवासीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Residential' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'BDO issues residence certificate to mother of ch' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'BDO issues residence certificate to mother of' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'BDO issues residence certificate to mother of' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off..." (Hinglish Arth: अमीना खातून और अब्दुल हबीब को जन्म प्रमाण पत्र के लिए आवश्यक निवास प्रमाण देने से इस आधार पर इनकार कर दिया गया कि अब्दुल हबीब का नाम एसआईआर के दौरान मतदाता सूची से हटा दिया गया था।)

articles.title: Karnataka Industries Minister holds talks with four Japanese companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans. According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive interior materials, discussions focused on its manufacturing operations at the Kadakola Industrial Area in Mysuru and its plans to expand its presence in line with Toyota’s growing capacity in the State. At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. Ltd., a Japanese manufacturer of precision connector components and semiconductor lead frames, discussions centred on potential expansion locations, including the Tumakuru Machine Tool Park and the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a meeting with representatives of Secom and Toyota Tsusho Corporation, the Minister discussed the growth plans of Sakra World Hospital. Discussions were also held with Makino, a leading manufacturer of high-precision machine tools, the release said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Karnataka Industries Minister holds talks with four Japanese companies

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:22:06 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans. According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive interior materials, discussions focused on its manufacturing operations at the Kadakola Industrial Area in Mysuru and its plans to expand its presence in line with Toyota’s growing capacity in the State. At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. Ltd., a Japanese manufacturer of precision connector components and semiconductor lead frames, discussions centred on potential expansion locations, including the Tumakuru Machine Tool Park and the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a meeting with representatives of Secom and Toyota Tsusho Corporation, the Minister discussed the growth plans of Sakra World Hospital. Discussions were also held with Makino, a leading manufacturer of high-precision machine tools, the release said.

articles.title: Leave aside any differences, remove BJP in U.P., says Congress chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) in Lucknow urged party leaders and workers to strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress alliance and leave aside any differences in a bid to oust the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh. “To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk. We have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power. Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow. Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”. Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Congress chief added, “Amit Shah said in Parliament, 'It has become fashionable to invoke Baba Saheb Ambedkar’s name. If you had invoked God’s name so much, you would have attained heaven.’ You people yourself are stealing in the name of Lord Ram; you are not going to get heaven”. Later, in the day Congress State unit leaders were detained while taking out Constitution Protection March. “We [Congressmen] were taking out the ‘Constitution Protection March’ peacefully and were detained, but our resolve to protect the Constitution became stronger. The place may change; the paths may be blocked, but the struggle to protect the Constitution has not stopped and will not stop,” said Anil Yadav, a senior Congress leader. Lucknow police took Congress leaders to Lucknow’s Eco Garden and freed in the evening. “The BJP government cannot tolerate even voices raised in support of the Constitution and democracy. The police force’s arrest of Congress leaders and workers who peacefully took to the streets, vowing to defend the Constitution, is deeply shameful. Is it now a crime to demand protection of our Constitution? “Remember, the repression of power cannot erase the values ​​of the Constitution, nor can it silence the voice of democracy. Congress will continue its struggle until the rights of every citizen, the power of every vote, and the Constitution are respected,” said Dwijendra Tripathi, a senior Congress worker based in Lucknow.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian National Congress / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / election

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Leave aside any differences, remove BJP in U.P., says Congress chief

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 04:09:06 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) in Lucknow urged party leaders and workers to strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress alliance and leave aside any differences in a bid to oust the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh. “To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk. We have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power. Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow. Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”. Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Congress chief added, “Amit Shah said in Parliament, 'It has become fashionable to invoke Baba Saheb Ambedkar’s name. If you had invoked God’s name so much, you would have attained heaven.’ You people yourself are stealing in the name of Lord Ram; you are not going to get heaven”. Later, in the day Congress State unit leaders were detained while taking out Constitution Protection March. “We [Congressmen] were taking out the ‘Constitution Protection March’ peacefully and were detained, but our resolve to protect the Constitution became stronger. The place may change; the paths may be blocked, but the struggle to protect the Constitution has not stopped and will not stop,” said Anil Yadav, a senior Congress leader. Lucknow police took Congress leaders to Lucknow’s Eco Garden and freed in the evening. “The BJP government cannot tolerate even voices raised in support of the Constitution and democracy. The police force’s arrest of Congress leaders and workers who peacefully took to the streets, vowing to defend the Constitution, is deeply shameful. Is it now a crime to demand protection of our Constitution? “Remember, the repression of power cannot erase the values ​​of the Constitution, nor can it silence the voice of democracy. Congress will continue its struggle until the rights of every citizen, the power of every vote, and the Constitution are respected,” said Dwijendra Tripathi, a senior Congress worker based in Lucknow.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian National Congress / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / election

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) in Lucknow urged party leaders and workers to strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress alliance and leave aside any differences in a bid to oust the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh. “To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk. We have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power. Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow. Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”. Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Congress chief added, “Amit Shah said in Parliament, 'It has become fashionable to invoke Baba Saheb Ambedkar’s name. If you had invoked God’s name so much, you would have attained heaven.’ You people yourself are stealing in the name of Lord Ram; you are not going to get heaven”. Later, in the day Congress State unit leaders were detained while taking out Constitution Protection March. “We [Congressmen] were taking out the ‘Constitution Protection March’ peacefully and were detained, but our resolve to protect the Constitution became stronger. The place may change; the paths may be blocked, but the struggle to protect the Constitution has not stopped and will not stop,” said Anil Yadav, a senior Congress leader. Lucknow police took Congress leaders to Lucknow’s Eco Garden and freed in the evening. “The BJP government cannot tolerate even voices raised in support of the Constitution and democracy. The police force’s arrest of Congress leaders and workers who peacefully took to the streets, vowing to defend the Constitution, is deeply shameful. Is it now a crime to demand protection of our Constitution? “Remember, the repression of power cannot erase the values ​​of the Constitution, nor can it silence the voice of democracy. Congress will continue its struggle until the rights of every citizen, the power of every vote, and the Constitution are respected,” said Dwijendra Tripathi, a senior Congress worker based in Lucknow.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian National Congress / Samajwadi Party / Bharatiya Janata Party / election

articles.title: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,’ Justice A.J. Bhambhani said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material. Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 “Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said. The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”. Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”. The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country. Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:59:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,’ Justice A.J. Bhambhani said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material. Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 “Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said. The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”. Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”. The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country. Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir’s selection board’s official X handle ‘suspended’ amid anti-board protests over cheating case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on November 25, 2026, apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The official X handle of the J&K Service Selection Board (JKSSB) was reportedly suspended on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as protests against the recruitment board continued in the wake of the recent case of cheating during the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination in Jammu. Meanwhile, activists and aspirants, who were seeking postponement of the Sub-Inspector examination, were allegedly detained in Jammu. Official sources said the official handle of the Board on X was suspended on Wednesday (November 25), apparently due to large-scale reporting by protesting netizens online. The JKSSB has not issued any statement on the suspension of its X handle. It had around 129.1K followers. Meanwhile, several aspirants held protests in Jammu against the Board and demanded postponement of the upcoming Police Sub-Inspector (PSI) examination scheduled for November 29. Meanwhile, the Board said it put in place fresh measures to check cheating. It has asked the Deputy Commissioners to appoint invigilation staff through a randomisation process, drawing from a pool of staff already identified. “Exam centres will be allotted to candidates at random, but admit cards will now be available for download only three days before the exam instead of seven,” it said. The magistrates have been tasked to supervise the frisking of candidates and exam staff. All staff deployed at a centre, including service providers, will have to hand in their mobile phones and other gadgets, which will be kept locked in the centre’s control room until the exam ends, it added. The Board also increased jammers at exam centres and pressed CCTV for live monitoring. Unsatisfied by the Board’s assurances, scores of aspirants held street protests in Jammu. Vinkal Sharma, an activist, said, “We demand postponement of the SI examination till the Board maintains transparency.” The J&K Students Association (JKSA) alleged that Mr. Sharma and over a dozen other protesters were detained by the police. “The detentions are deeply unfortunate and unjustified. It is an attempt to suppress legitimate democratic dissent. All detained students and aspirants should be released,” said the Association. Former Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah, in a post on X, said, “Enough of this blame game between the two power centres. They must stop passing responsibility and start acting. Postpone the November 29 JKPSI examination and constitute an independent SIT to probe the alleged JKSSB FAA irregularities. They are demanding justice, transparency and accountability. Their future cannot be held hostage to administrative failures.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On November 15, the J&K Police busted four “cheating modules” in Jammu during the Board’s examination for the FAA posts. Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K. The Board has faced more than three major allegations of scams during recruitment examinations in the past six years.
