🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 200-year-old Taj Mahal marble slab to be auctioned in U.K.

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:44:53 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The rectangular slab is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An intricate floral-bordered marble slab taken from the Taj Mahal in Agra by an officer of the East India Company is set to be auctioned in the U.K. next month. The rectangular slab, one of two that Colonel Pownoll Phipps collected in 1816 at the end of his tenure as superintendent of the repairs of the buildings in and around Agra, is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately). It is being offered as part of the Islamic and Indian Art sale by Lyon and Turnbull auctioneers on December 9. “The marble slab is accompanied by a vintage black and white photograph of the Taj Mahal and two letters — one printed by the grandson of Colonel Pownoll and one handwritten by the Marquess of Bath,” the auction notes state. The colonel’s son's memoirs quote that his father found them in a ‘souterrain’, or underground area, at the Taj Mahal and that he thought they were intended for the repairs to the iconic Mughal-era monument. Colonel Pownoll Phipps was born in Devon, England, in 1780. Hailing from a line of soldiers since the early 17th century, he joined the East India Company as a cadet in the Bengal Army in 1799. After battling troops in Egypt, Phipps returned to India, where he quickly rose through the ranks, becoming Fort-Adjutant and Barrack-Master at Agra in 1809, where he remained for the next seven years. During the colonial era, he was responsible among other things for the care of the Taj Mahal and other historic buildings. “He took this job most seriously and was at times called upon to prevent damage by Europeans looking for keepsakes. As his son wrote, ‘he was once sent for to the Taj, where, in spite of the remonstrances of the sentry, an English lady was insisting on picking agates out of the marble with a steel fork’,” the auctioneers note.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 1816, the colonel was chosen by the Governor General of India to become Superintendent of Building in the Lower Provinces, which meant leaving Agra for Kolkata.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "200-year-old Taj Mahal marble slab to be auctioned in U.K.", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The rectangular slab is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately)." D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Supreme Court declares authorities 'wilfully disobeyed' court orders, suspends Board of Trustees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The apex court issues show cause notices on contempt against Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and Trustees

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court ordered the Chief Secretary to explain why the constitutional duty to aid the Supreme Court was not followed and explain the “apparent disregard”. The court gives the Chief Secretary 10 days to respond. If the current flame is not burning, the Supreme Court allows independent arrangements to be made. The court orders all alleged contemnors to be present in person on the next date of hearing, December 15. This order [lighting the lamp tomorrow] would not create any equities in favour of any parties, said Justice Kumar. The Supreme Court directs the temple receivers to light the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar on November 28 after consultations with Sthanikars. The lamp is to be lit from the flame, if it is still burning. Worshippers shall be allowed to light their lamps on the hill. Cordon off 50 m from the dargah. No devotee to the dargah should be affected or stopped. Central forces and CRPF personnel were asked to provide security. The Supreme Court issued show-cause notices on contempt against the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and the Trustees. It also declared that the Board of Trustees has been suspended. The temple has been handed over to receivers, former High Court judges, Justice S. Vaidyanathan and S. Parthiban. The Collector had tendered a formal apology, attempted to shift the blame entirely to the devasthanam . Surprised that a collector is taking this stance, his powers are wide enought to implement the orders of this court.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: We are not satisfied with his preliminary report. Have to see whether his account reflects what happened. The stand of the Collector reminds of “pretending to cry”.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Supreme Court declares authorities 'wilfully disobeyed' court orders, suspends Board of Trustees

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:16:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The apex court issues show cause notices on contempt against Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and Trustees

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court ordered the Chief Secretary to explain why the constitutional duty to aid the Supreme Court was not followed and explain the “apparent disregard”. The court gives the Chief Secretary 10 days to respond. If the current flame is not burning, the Supreme Court allows independent arrangements to be made. The court orders all alleged contemnors to be present in person on the next date of hearing, December 15. This order [lighting the lamp tomorrow] would not create any equities in favour of any parties, said Justice Kumar. The Supreme Court directs the temple receivers to light the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar on November 28 after consultations with Sthanikars. The lamp is to be lit from the flame, if it is still burning. Worshippers shall be allowed to light their lamps on the hill. Cordon off 50 m from the dargah. No devotee to the dargah should be affected or stopped. Central forces and CRPF personnel were asked to provide security. The Supreme Court issued show-cause notices on contempt against the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and the Trustees. It also declared that the Board of Trustees has been suspended. The temple has been handed over to receivers, former High Court judges, Justice S. Vaidyanathan and S. Parthiban. The Collector had tendered a formal apology, attempted to shift the blame entirely to the devasthanam . Surprised that a collector is taking this stance, his powers are wide enought to implement the orders of this court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: We are not satisfied with his preliminary report. Have to see whether his account reflects what happened. The stand of the Collector reminds of “pretending to cry”.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Security (Noun)
सुरक्षा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Security' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Supreme Court declares authorities 'wilfully disobeyed' court orders, suspends Board of Trustees", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The apex court issues show cause notices on contempt against Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Suprem' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Sup' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Sup' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The apex court issues show cause notices on contempt against Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, HR&CE Commissioner, Board of Trustees Chairperson and..." (Hinglish Arth: शीर्ष अदालत ने तमिलनाडु के मुख्य सचिव, डीजीपी, मानव संसाधन और सीई आयुक्त, न्यासी बोर्ड के अध्यक्ष और न्यासियों के खिलाफ अवमानना ​​पर कारण बताओ नोटिस जारी किया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Supreme Court declares authorities 'wilfully disobeyed' court orders, suspends Board of Trustees"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The stand of the Collector reminds of “pretending to cry”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The stand of the Collector reminds of “pretending to cry”." (Hinglish Arth: कलेक्टर का रुख "रोने का नाटक" की याद दिलाता है।)

articles.title: Suspected JeM operative held in Vadodara; planned to attack IAF station, says ATS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, says ATS DIG Sunil Josh

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative with an assault weapon and ammunition in Vadodara, foiling an alleged plot to attack the Indian Air Force (IAF) station in the city, officials said on Friday (November 27, 2026). The accused, Mohommad Saharul Islam Kabiruddin, a resident of Karimganj in Assam, was apprehended near a hotel on Halol-Vadodara Road on Thursday (November 26) night based on technical and human intelligence inputs, ATS Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Sunil Joshi said. The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, he said. During interrogation, it came to light that the accused was allegedly tasked with attacking the gate of the IAF station in Vadodara, and photographs of the establishment were recovered from his mobile phone, the official said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A case has been registered against him under relevant provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), officials added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Suspected JeM operative held in Vadodara; planned to attack IAF station, says ATS

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:15:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, says ATS DIG Sunil Josh

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative with an assault weapon and ammunition in Vadodara, foiling an alleged plot to attack the Indian Air Force (IAF) station in the city, officials said on Friday (November 27, 2026). The accused, Mohommad Saharul Islam Kabiruddin, a resident of Karimganj in Assam, was apprehended near a hotel on Halol-Vadodara Road on Thursday (November 26) night based on technical and human intelligence inputs, ATS Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Sunil Joshi said. The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, he said. During interrogation, it came to light that the accused was allegedly tasked with attacking the gate of the IAF station in Vadodara, and photographs of the establishment were recovered from his mobile phone, the official said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A case has been registered against him under relevant provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), officials added.

articles.title: Odisha’s interest must be protected: BJD on delimitation bill
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The regional party says the party will come up with a formal stand once details of bill to be discussed in Parliament is made available

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Biju Janata Dal on Friday (November 27, 2026) said it would decide its stand on the amended delimitation bill in the Rajya Sabha after receiving complete information, asserting that Odisha’s interests would remain its sole priority in taking a call on the issue. The party issued a statement saying that discussions on delimitation had once again begun following the announcement of special sessions of the Lok Sabha on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, 2026. Manas Mangaraj, Leader of the BJD Parliamentary Party in the Rajya Sabha, said the party had not yet received any information regarding the specific issues to be discussed during the upcoming special sessions. “After receiving detailed facts and information in this regard, the Parliamentary Party will take further steps as per the directions of BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik. The BJD has always given priority to the interests of the State and will never deviate from this principle in the future either,” Mr. Mangaraj said, without divulging the party’s position on the different formulas being speculated upon for delimitation. Meanwhile, BJD Rajya Sabha member Santrupta Mishra, while speaking to the media, said the party had always maintained that Odisha’s present proportion of representation in Parliament must be protected. The proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in Parliament for different States, which was being discussed in various forums, did not necessarily ensure equity, he pointed out. Mr. Mishra said Odisha’s interests, or those of smaller States, should not be compromised. Until the details of the bill were made available, it would be difficult for the BJD to take a stand, the Rajya Sabha MP said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At present, the BJD has five MPs in Rajya Sabha while it has no representation in Lok Sabha.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Odisha’s interest must be protected: BJD on delimitation bill

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 05:15:51 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The regional party says the party will come up with a formal stand once details of bill to be discussed in Parliament is made available

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Biju Janata Dal on Friday (November 27, 2026) said it would decide its stand on the amended delimitation bill in the Rajya Sabha after receiving complete information, asserting that Odisha’s interests would remain its sole priority in taking a call on the issue. The party issued a statement saying that discussions on delimitation had once again begun following the announcement of special sessions of the Lok Sabha on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, 2026. Manas Mangaraj, Leader of the BJD Parliamentary Party in the Rajya Sabha, said the party had not yet received any information regarding the specific issues to be discussed during the upcoming special sessions. “After receiving detailed facts and information in this regard, the Parliamentary Party will take further steps as per the directions of BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik. The BJD has always given priority to the interests of the State and will never deviate from this principle in the future either,” Mr. Mangaraj said, without divulging the party’s position on the different formulas being speculated upon for delimitation. Meanwhile, BJD Rajya Sabha member Santrupta Mishra, while speaking to the media, said the party had always maintained that Odisha’s present proportion of representation in Parliament must be protected. The proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in Parliament for different States, which was being discussed in various forums, did not necessarily ensure equity, he pointed out. Mr. Mishra said Odisha’s interests, or those of smaller States, should not be compromised. Until the details of the bill were made available, it would be difficult for the BJD to take a stand, the Rajya Sabha MP said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At present, the BJD has five MPs in Rajya Sabha while it has no representation in Lok Sabha.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Biju Janata Dal on Friday (November 27, 2026) said it would decide its stand on the amended delimitation bill in the Rajya Sabha after receiving complete information, asserting that Odisha’s interests would remain its sole priority in taking a call on the issue. The proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in Parliament for different States, which was being discussed in various forums, did not necessarily ensure equity, he pointed out. Mr. Mishra said Odisha’s interests, or those of smaller States, should not be compromised. Until the details of the bill were made available, it would be difficult for the BJD to take a stand, the Rajya Sabha MP said.

articles.title: CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated newspapers in jails, questioning whether a “super Emergency” had been declared in Keralam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior party leader M V Jayarajan told reporters in Kannur that a circular directing prisons to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers, including Deshabhimani , the CPI(M)’s mouthpiece, was issued by the Director General of Prisons a day ago. “Has a super Emergency been declared in Keralam? Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said. Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said. There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged. He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them. The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister. His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties. In a circular issued on Thursday, Director General of Prisons S Sreejith said correctional institutions, which aim at the psychological and social rehabilitation of inmates, should ensure that the news and information made available to them were objective, truthful and free from political bias.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution in prisons, the circular said.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:11:43 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated newspapers in jails, questioning whether a “super Emergency” had been declared in Keralam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior party leader M V Jayarajan told reporters in Kannur that a circular directing prisons to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers, including Deshabhimani , the CPI(M)’s mouthpiece, was issued by the Director General of Prisons a day ago. “Has a super Emergency been declared in Keralam? Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said. Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said. There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged. He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them. The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister. His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties. articles.title: NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam. The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State. The amicus curiae made the observations based on the affidavits and compliance reports submitted by the authorities. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day, it said. The amicus curiae pointed out that inert waste is being used for land filling without safeguards. Quoting a report submitted by the Keralam government, the report said that about 404.8 tonnes per day of inert waste is used for filling up appropriate portions of hilly areas, stadiums, railway platforms, yards and road embankment formations. No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested. The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone. The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said. The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

hinglishTracks.en: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — रिपोर्ट में नदियों, बैकवाटर, तालाबों और समुद्र में सीवेज ले जाने वाले नालों, झरनों और तूफानी जल चैनलों की जीआईएस-मैप सूची तैयार करने का सुझाव दिया गया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Preparation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: तैयारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Preparation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:09:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A report filed by an amicus curiae appointed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has flagged multiple gaps in the management of solid and liquid waste in Keralam. The deficiencies have been pointed out in the observation note dated November 24, 2026 submitted in the matter related to the compliance of Municipal Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 and other environmental issues in the State. The amicus curiae made the observations based on the affidavits and compliance reports submitted by the authorities. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated. Only 42.1 tonnes per day of the total sanitary waste of 203.66 tonnes generated daily is treated. Even when all projects are complete, the capacity will be 113.25 tonnes per day, it said. The amicus curiae pointed out that inert waste is being used for land filling without safeguards. Quoting a report submitted by the Keralam government, the report said that about 404.8 tonnes per day of inert waste is used for filling up appropriate portions of hilly areas, stadiums, railway platforms, yards and road embankment formations. No register of sites, test reports or approvals is given. Given the State’s wetlands and landslide-prone slopes, this practice needs strict control, it suggested. The report said that the action on the illegal drains discharging untreated sewage into streams and water bodies has been initiated in only four districts, including Kollam, Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Kottayam as per the affidavit submitted by the government. Of the 723 illegal outlets in the four districts, 671 are in Ernakulam alone. The total quantity of processed and unprocessed legacy (old) waste has increased from 19.54 lakh metric tonnes in December 2025 to 19,6 lakh metric tonnes in July 2026. The gap in total sewage generated and treated is as high as 3901.2 million litres daily, indicative of a serious concern, it said. The amicus curiae has suggested a sample-based functional audit of composting bins and biogas plants. The four regional plants for sanitary waste treatment should be commissioned by a fixed date. For inert and land filling, a register of every site where inert are used for filling be maintained and published, with test reports and approvals.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds and the sea.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Quantitative (Adjective)
आंकड़ों और संख्या पर आधारित — जिसे ठोस नंबरों और डेटा में मापा जा सके।
✓ Syn: Measurable, Numerical, Empirical  |  ✖ Ant: Qualitative, Subjective, Unmeasurable
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Observation (Noun)
अवलोकन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Observation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Preparation (Noun)
तैयारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Preparation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Kerala' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Ker' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Ker' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The report stated that about four-fifths of sanitary waste is not scientifically treated." (Hinglish Arth: रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि लगभग चार-पाँचवें सैनिटरी कचरे का वैज्ञानिक तरीके से उपचार नहीं किया जाता है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "NGT-appointed amicus report flags gaps in Keralam’s solid, liquid waste management"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The report suggested preparation of a GIS-mapped inventory of drains, streams and storm-water channels carrying sewage into rivers, backwaters, ponds..." (Hinglish Arth: रिपोर्ट में नदियों, बैकवाटर, तालाबों और समुद्र में सीवेज ले जाने वाले नालों, झरनों और तूफानी जल चैनलों की जीआईएस-मैप सूची तैयार करने का सुझाव दिया गया है।)

articles.title: Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme on Thursday (November 27, 2026) to extend food-security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries, asserting that his government has ensured that only the genuinely needy would receive their rightful entitlements through a transparent selection process. Along with Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal , Mr. Mann distributed "Meri Rasoi" kits among beneficiaries on stage at an event in Moga. The kits contained pulses, sugar, salt, turmeric and mustard oil. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC. "Our government has undertaken a special drive to issue 10 lakh new ration cards to the most deserving and needy families. The entire exercise has been conducted through a digital, transparent and impartial system to ensure that genuine beneficiaries receive their rightful entitlements, without any discrimination or political interference," he said. Mr. Mann noted that 19.25 lakh online applications were received during the special campaign launched in July. "People applied through sewa kendras, common service centres (CSCs) and online platforms, while the district administration conducted door-to-door verification to identify eligible families," he said. Mr. Mann said that under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, Punjab currently has 1.36 crore beneficiaries belonging to 39.73 lakh families. "All new ration card beneficiaries will receive a special Meri Rasoi kit comprising two kg of pulses, two kg of sugar, one kg of salt, 200 of grams turmeric powder and one litre mustard oil. Besides, they will continue to receive free wheat under the National Food Security Act," he said. The AAP government in Punjab is committed to ensuring food security for every deserving family, the Chief Minister said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections of the society, he added.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:09:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann launched the Smart Ration Card Scheme on Thursday (November 27, 2026) to extend food-security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries, asserting that his government has ensured that only the genuinely needy would receive their rightful entitlements through a transparent selection process. Along with Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal , Mr. Mann distributed "Meri Rasoi" kits among beneficiaries on stage at an event in Moga. The kits contained pulses, sugar, salt, turmeric and mustard oil. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC. "Our government has undertaken a special drive to issue 10 lakh new ration cards to the most deserving and needy families. The entire exercise has been conducted through a digital, transparent and impartial system to ensure that genuine beneficiaries receive their rightful entitlements, without any discrimination or political interference," he said. Mr. Mann noted that 19.25 lakh online applications were received during the special campaign launched in July. "People applied through sewa kendras, common service centres (CSCs) and online platforms, while the district administration conducted door-to-door verification to identify eligible families," he said. Mr. Mann said that under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, Punjab currently has 1.36 crore beneficiaries belonging to 39.73 lakh families. "All new ration card beneficiaries will receive a special Meri Rasoi kit comprising two kg of pulses, two kg of sugar, one kg of salt, 200 of grams turmeric powder and one litre mustard oil. Besides, they will continue to receive free wheat under the National Food Security Act," he said. The AAP government in Punjab is committed to ensuring food security for every deserving family, the Chief Minister said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections of the society, he added.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Discrimination (Adjective / Verb)
भेदभाव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Discrimination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Interference (Adjective / Verb)
दखल अंदाजी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Interference' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Verification (Noun)
सत्यापन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Verification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to b' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme t' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme t' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Chief Minister assured the beneficiaries of five kg of free wheat per family member per month after the completion of e-KYC." (Hinglish Arth: मुख्यमंत्री ने लाभार्थियों को ई-केवाईसी पूरी होने के बाद प्रति माह प्रति परिवार के सदस्य को पांच किलो गेहूं मुफ्त देने का आश्वासन दिया)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Punjab CM launches Smart Ration Card Scheme to benefit 10 lakh beneficiaries"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "These additional benefits will provide meaningful relief to ordinary households and strengthen the welfare support extended to the poorest sections..." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा कि ये अतिरिक्त लाभ सामान्य परिवारों को सार्थक राहत प्रदान करेंगे और समाज के सबसे गरीब वर्गों को दी जाने वाली कल्याणकारी सहायता को मजबूत करेंगे।)

articles.title: Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pakistan is set to host talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday (November 27, 2026) under a trilateral defence pact that treats an attack on any member as an attack on all three, two security officials said. The talks in Islamabad will focus on developments in West Asia, including ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels , the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the meeting publicly. Pakistan has said that the agreement is purely defensive in nature and not against anyone, including Iran, and that the trilateral alliance reflects a shared desire to strengthen strategic security cooperation. Senior diplomats as well as defence and military officials from the three countries are expected to discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties, the officials said. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir will attend the meeting. Mr. Asif has said that Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks from the Houthis. However, Pakistan is still making efforts, with help from countries in West Asia, including Qatar, to urge the United States and Iran to return to the negotiating table to end the conflict in the region and beyond through talks. Pakistan had brokered an interim deal between the two sides in June 2026. Friday’s meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee falls under the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, which was signed in August 2026 in the Saudi holy city of Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Pakistan’s government has not released details ahead of the meeting, but the authorities have declared a local holiday in Islamabad to limit public movement as part of security measures for the gathering. Islamabad traffic police have announced road diversions and advised motorists to use alternative routes to accommodate the movement of foreign delegations. During a previous meeting in Riyadh, the three sides had vowed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed-upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the agreement, the group’s secretariat has been established in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will also attend Friday’s meeting. The pact binds the parties for 10 years, after which they would need to give three months’ notice before leaving.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:51:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pakistan is set to host talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday (November 27, 2026) under a trilateral defence pact that treats an attack on any member as an attack on all three, two security officials said. The talks in Islamabad will focus on developments in West Asia, including ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels , the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the meeting publicly. Pakistan has said that the agreement is purely defensive in nature and not against anyone, including Iran, and that the trilateral alliance reflects a shared desire to strengthen strategic security cooperation. Senior diplomats as well as defence and military officials from the three countries are expected to discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties, the officials said. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir will attend the meeting. Mr. Asif has said that Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks from the Houthis. However, Pakistan is still making efforts, with help from countries in West Asia, including Qatar, to urge the United States and Iran to return to the negotiating table to end the conflict in the region and beyond through talks. Pakistan had brokered an interim deal between the two sides in June 2026. Friday’s meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee falls under the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, which was signed in August 2026 in the Saudi holy city of Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. Pakistan’s government has not released details ahead of the meeting, but the authorities have declared a local holiday in Islamabad to limit public movement as part of security measures for the gathering. Islamabad traffic police have announced road diversions and advised motorists to use alternative routes to accommodate the movement of foreign delegations. During a previous meeting in Riyadh, the three sides had vowed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed-upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the agreement, the group’s secretariat has been established in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will also attend Friday’s meeting. The pact binds the parties for 10 years, after which they would need to give three months’ notice before leaving.

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Cooperation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Alternative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Alternative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and..."

articles.title: Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 01:21:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine. "During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network. Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly." "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added. The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week. In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war." In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Elevated blood sugar during adulthood linked with worse cognition in midlife: study

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 03:25:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades. The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought. Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association . "Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said. "However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said. The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health. Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes. "The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said. "This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Parenting in an anxious age: What does ‘good enough’ look like?

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 02:37:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai. Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent. As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders. Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents? Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Hindu Sunday Magazine / children / parent and child / technology (general) / OpenAI / Artificial Intelligence / human interest

articles.title: Himachal BJP demands re-exam after Sikh youth barred from patwari exam over kara, kirpan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The State BJP’s Minority Morcha chief asked the Congress government to explain the incident at an examination centre in Solan and to hold a special examination for the candidate

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Himachal Pradesh unit of the BJP on Friday (November 27, 2026) demanded a re-examination for the patwari post exclusively for an Amritdhari (baptised) Sikh candidate who was allegedly barred from appearing in the exam over his kara and kirpan . Addressing the media in Poanta Sahib in Sirmaur district, State BJP Minority Morcha chief Gurmeet Singh sought an explanation from the Congress government over the incident at the ‘Devbhoomi Online Examination Centre’ in Solan. He demanded that the State government conduct an inquiry, hold a special patwari (revenue official) examination for the affected candidate, and amend the examination guidelines so that no candidate is deprived of taking an exam because of their religious beliefs. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said the matter concerned not only the future of a student but also his religious freedom and constitutional rights. He said he had spoken to the candidate, who told him he had been asked to remove his kara (iron/steel bangle) and kirpan (ceremonial sword). The Sikh youth told him that the examination centre operator cited “government instructions” for disallowing those articles, but when asked for the relevant notification, the authorities failed to provide a copy, he said. The candidate’s father, Vichitra Singh, who was also present at the press conference, demanded that the government clarify the specific order under which the candidate was barred from the examination. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said a father invests his hard-earned money in his child’s education, dreaming of a bright future for him, and being barred from the examination had come as a severe blow to the family. Referring to Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to religious freedom, he said carrying a kirpan is an integral part of the Sikh faith, and that while establishing security protocols for examinations, constitutional rights and religious beliefs must be respected. He also raised concerns about alleged restrictions on mangalsutras (sacred necklaces) and bangles worn by women under the examination guidelines, and urged the government to review directives that interfere with religious and cultural practices.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The patwari recruitment examinations began on November 23, 2026, and are scheduled to conclude on November 30, 2026.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The patwari recruitment examinations began on November 23, 2026, and are scheduled to conclude on November 30, 2026.

hinglishTracks.en: The Himachal Pradesh unit of the BJP on Friday (November 27, 2026) demanded a re-examination for the patwari post exclusively for an Amritdhari (baptised) Sikh candidate who was allegedly barred from appearing in the exam over his kara and kirpan .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — भाजपा की हिमाचल प्रदेश इकाई ने शुक्रवार (नवंबर 27, 2026) को विशेष रूप से एक अमृतधारी (बपतिस्मा प्राप्त) सिख उम्मीदवार के लिए पटवारी पद के लिए पुन: परीक्षा की मांग की, जिसे कथित तौर पर कड़ा और कृपाण के कारण परीक्षा में बैठने से रोक दिया गया था।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Examination' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: परीक्षा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Examination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Addressing the media in Poanta Sahib in Sirmaur district, State BJP Minority Morcha chief Gurmeet Singh sought an explanation from the Congress government over the incident at the ‘Devbhoomi Online Examination Centre’ in Solan.

📰 Himachal BJP demands re-exam after Sikh youth barred from patwari exam over kara, kirpan

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 05:23:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The State BJP’s Minority Morcha chief asked the Congress government to explain the incident at an examination centre in Solan and to hold a special examination for the candidate

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Himachal Pradesh unit of the BJP on Friday (November 27, 2026) demanded a re-examination for the patwari post exclusively for an Amritdhari (baptised) Sikh candidate who was allegedly barred from appearing in the exam over his kara and kirpan . Addressing the media in Poanta Sahib in Sirmaur district, State BJP Minority Morcha chief Gurmeet Singh sought an explanation from the Congress government over the incident at the ‘Devbhoomi Online Examination Centre’ in Solan. He demanded that the State government conduct an inquiry, hold a special patwari (revenue official) examination for the affected candidate, and amend the examination guidelines so that no candidate is deprived of taking an exam because of their religious beliefs. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said the matter concerned not only the future of a student but also his religious freedom and constitutional rights. He said he had spoken to the candidate, who told him he had been asked to remove his kara (iron/steel bangle) and kirpan (ceremonial sword). The Sikh youth told him that the examination centre operator cited “government instructions” for disallowing those articles, but when asked for the relevant notification, the authorities failed to provide a copy, he said. The candidate’s father, Vichitra Singh, who was also present at the press conference, demanded that the government clarify the specific order under which the candidate was barred from the examination. Mr. Gurmeet Singh said a father invests his hard-earned money in his child’s education, dreaming of a bright future for him, and being barred from the examination had come as a severe blow to the family. Referring to Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees the right to religious freedom, he said carrying a kirpan is an integral part of the Sikh faith, and that while establishing security protocols for examinations, constitutional rights and religious beliefs must be respected. He also raised concerns about alleged restrictions on mangalsutras (sacred necklaces) and bangles worn by women under the examination guidelines, and urged the government to review directives that interfere with religious and cultural practices.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The patwari recruitment examinations began on November 23, 2026, and are scheduled to conclude on November 30, 2026.

articles.title: IBM ends U.S. visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in consulting unit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programmes to address skill shortages,’ the company said in a statement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Global tech giant IBM is discontinuing U.S. visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting business, its largest division with over 150,000 employees. The move comes at a time when companies based in the U.S. are increasingly facing pressure from the government over their use of work visas and reliance on foreign workers. "IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programmes to address skill shortages. That participation has been declining for several years, and as skill availability and client needs have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting,” the company said in a statement. While the tech giant didn't offer further details, affected employees have reportedly been offered a choice between relocating to a country outside the U.S. or leaving the company by the end of the year. According to posts by employees on the anonymous professional discussion platform Blind, some affected employees have been given about three weeks to decide, with three months' severance for those who decline an overseas role and December 31 as their last working day, “I got pulled into a surprise meeting with my manager and was told I have just three weeks to choose between taking an 80% pay cut to relocate to India or losing my job by December 31. I've spent years building my career here, working long hours for IBM clients, paying taxes and building a life in the U.S. Now I'm being told to either uproot everything or walk away with just three months of severance,” an employee wrote on Blind. Over the past years, U.S. tech giants have faced increased scrutiny over reliance on foreign workers, deepening the uncertainty for an industry where employees across companies are facing the threat of AI displacement. In September 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump extended the $100,000 fee on employers for bringing in foreign workers on H-1B visas. He said the 2025 decision to impose a $100,000 fee has led to a 92% decrease in H-1B registrations by large IT outsourcing firms. An extension of the 2025 Proclamation will continue to protect the economic and national security interests of the United States, improve labour market access for American workers and graduates, and ensure that employers recruit only the most highly skilled and essential alien workers when needed in line with the original intent of the programme, Mr. Trump said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indians remain the single largest beneficiary group of the U.S. H-1B visa programme.
