articles.title: Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Science-based diplomacy could aid India-Pakistan bilateral engagement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The economic and diplomatic consequences of India’s efforts to estrange Pakistan often overshadow the costs distributed between them. For example, Pakistani space scientists can today access facilities in China whereas Indian space scientists can access facilities in the United States and Europe . But Indian scientists studying environmental conditions in Pakistan and Pakistani scientists studying conditions in India have far fewer alternatives. The latter matters much more for regional development and stability. On November 25, Beijing’s ‘Space Silk Road’ diplomacy and the strain on New Delhi’s hedging strategies converged in the Shenzhou-24 mission as China launched Pakistan’s first astronaut , Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong space station. Pakistan had offered in 2015 to contribute to India’s proposed SAARC satellite and wanted the project administered under SAARC, but India insisted on operating it as largesse to its neighbours. If it had really been SAARC’s satellite, ISRO and its Pakistani counterpart, SUPARCO , could have developed an institutional relationship and India could have influenced its neighbour’s space programme through a multilateral mechanism. But today, India’s ability to engage Pakistan on regional matters has increasingly depended on negotiating with powers beyond South Asia, in institutions with other agendas. Even as spaceflight emerges as a new geopolitical realm, its substantial scientific component affords countries opportunities to engage independently of interstate relations in other domains. The Shenzhou-24 experience will be significant for SUPARCO just as the Axiom-4 mission in the U.S. was for ISRO , helping to significantly lower Islamabad’s cost to access similar future opportunities, especially those under the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization, which also includes Bangladesh, and the Belt and Road Initiative’s Space Information Corridor . There is no question that Indian spaceflight is technologically superior to that of Pakistan, but the Shenzhou-24 mission is a reminder that China’s technological superiority vis-à-vis India’s leaves India with an unequal contest. India has been ceding the neighbourhood to China’s space networks, and by squandering the opportunities afforded by science diplomacy, it has left Pakistan to look to China even on problems it shares with India. The Apollo-Soyuz interaction during the Cold War and India and Pakistan working together to respond to a locust outbreak barely a year after the Balakot crisis (2019) are testament to the ability of science-based diplomacy to clear room for bilateral engagement with guardrails, without compromising the counter-terrorism agenda. India should revive such engagement.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Pakistan / China / space programme / USA / European / SAARC / ISRO / Asia / Bangladesh / Belt and Road Initiative / Balakot Air Strikes / diplomacy

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #2 of 30 (27 NOV)

📰 Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut

📌 Published: 27 Nov 2026, 11:58:06 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Science-based diplomacy could aid India-Pakistan bilateral engagement

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The economic and diplomatic consequences of India’s efforts to estrange Pakistan often overshadow the costs distributed between them. For example, Pakistani space scientists can today access facilities in China whereas Indian space scientists can access facilities in the United States and Europe . But Indian scientists studying environmental conditions in Pakistan and Pakistani scientists studying conditions in India have far fewer alternatives. The latter matters much more for regional development and stability. On November 25, Beijing’s ‘Space Silk Road’ diplomacy and the strain on New Delhi’s hedging strategies converged in the Shenzhou-24 mission as China launched Pakistan’s first astronaut , Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong space station. Pakistan had offered in 2015 to contribute to India’s proposed SAARC satellite and wanted the project administered under SAARC, but India insisted on operating it as largesse to its neighbours. If it had really been SAARC’s satellite, ISRO and its Pakistani counterpart, SUPARCO , could have developed an institutional relationship and India could have influenced its neighbour’s space programme through a multilateral mechanism. But today, India’s ability to engage Pakistan on regional matters has increasingly depended on negotiating with powers beyond South Asia, in institutions with other agendas. Even as spaceflight emerges as a new geopolitical realm, its substantial scientific component affords countries opportunities to engage independently of interstate relations in other domains. The Shenzhou-24 experience will be significant for SUPARCO just as the Axiom-4 mission in the U.S. was for ISRO , helping to significantly lower Islamabad’s cost to access similar future opportunities, especially those under the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization, which also includes Bangladesh, and the Belt and Road Initiative’s Space Information Corridor . There is no question that Indian spaceflight is technologically superior to that of Pakistan, but the Shenzhou-24 mission is a reminder that China’s technological superiority vis-à-vis India’s leaves India with an unequal contest. India has been ceding the neighbourhood to China’s space networks, and by squandering the opportunities afforded by science diplomacy, it has left Pakistan to look to China even on problems it shares with India. The Apollo-Soyuz interaction during the Cold War and India and Pakistan working together to respond to a locust outbreak barely a year after the Balakot crisis (2019) are testament to the ability of science-based diplomacy to clear room for bilateral engagement with guardrails, without compromising the counter-terrorism agenda. India should revive such engagement.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India / Pakistan / China / space programme / USA / European / SAARC / ISRO / Asia / Bangladesh / Belt and Road Initiative / Balakot Air Strikes / diplomacy

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Multilateral (Adjective)
बहुपक्षीय — जिसमें दो से अधिक देश (जैसे UN, G20, BRICS) मिलकर साझा फैसला लेते हैं।
✓ Syn: Plurilateral, International, Coalition-based  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, One-sided, Isolated
Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Science-based diplomacy could aid India-Pakistan bilateral engagement.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s fir' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Science-based diplomacy could aid India-Pakistan bilateral engagement." (Hinglish Arth: विज्ञान-आधारित कूटनीति भारत-पाकिस्तान द्विपक्षीय संबंधों में सहायता कर सकती है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Lifting off: on China’s launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. India / Pakistan / China / space programme / USA / European / SAARC / ISRO / Asia / Bangladesh / Belt and Road Initiative / Balakot Air Strikes /...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "India / Pakistan / China / space programme / USA / European / SAARC / ISRO / Asia / Bangladesh / Belt and Road Initiative / Balakot Air Strikes /..." (Hinglish Arth: भारत/पाकिस्तान/चीन/अंतरिक्ष कार्यक्रम/अमेरिका/यूरोपीय/सार्क/इसरो/एशिया/बांग्लादेश/बेल्ट एंड रोड पहल/बालाकोट हवाई हमले/कूटनीति)

articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. articles.title: G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:52:41 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।

Miscalculation (Noun)
अशुद्ध गणना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Miscalculation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Announcement (Adjective)
घोषणा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Announcement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts an' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O." (Hinglish Arth: सीएएस के लिए अपनाए जाने वाले पात्रता मानदंड और प्रक्रियाओं को जी.ओ. के माध्यम से जारी दिशानिर्देशों के 'सख्ती से पालन' में लागू किया जाएगा।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials." articles.title: Man arrested for murdering his wife over family dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the arrested person as K. Hariprasad. Initial inquiry revealed that Hariprasad was married to Krithika nearly a decade ago. The couple has two children. Police said that Hariprasad was working as a driver. The couple reportedly fought repeatedly over poor income to maintain the family. In recent months, police said that Hariprasad was also irregular at work, forcing Krithika to meet the entire needs of the family on her own. Police said that Krithika left her husband and stayed in her parents house with her children. Hariprasad repeatedly requested her live with him but she refused. Police said on Wednesday, Hariprasad met her again and asked to come along with him to his house. As she refused, enraged Hariprasad stabbed Krithika, who collapsed in a pool of blood, police said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on an alert from neighbours, the Sathuvachari police rushed to the spot and arrested Hariprasad. A case was registered and further probe is under way.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Man arrested for murdering his wife over family dispute

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:35:56 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the arrested person as K. Hariprasad. Initial inquiry revealed that Hariprasad was married to Krithika nearly a decade ago. The couple has two children. Police said that Hariprasad was working as a driver. The couple reportedly fought repeatedly over poor income to maintain the family. In recent months, police said that Hariprasad was also irregular at work, forcing Krithika to meet the entire needs of the family on her own. Police said that Krithika left her husband and stayed in her parents house with her children. Hariprasad repeatedly requested her live with him but she refused. Police said on Wednesday, Hariprasad met her again and asked to come along with him to his house. As she refused, enraged Hariprasad stabbed Krithika, who collapsed in a pool of blood, police said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on an alert from neighbours, the Sathuvachari police rushed to the spot and arrested Hariprasad. A case was registered and further probe is under way.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Man arrested for murdering his wife over family dispute", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Man arrested for murdering his wife over family ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Man arrested for murdering his wife over fami' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Man arrested for murdering his wife over fami' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute." ✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "A case was registered and further probe is under way." (Hinglish Arth: मामला दर्ज कर लिया गया है और आगे की जांच की जा रही है।)

articles.title: Burglars decamp with 15 sovereigns of gold, cash from house near Jolarpet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Burglars decamped with 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery, and around ₹1.2 lakh in cash from the house of a tribal family near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the victim as R. Siva, who belongs to the Irular community. He was living with his wife and son on the outskirts of the town. Siva went to Tiruvannamalai town for Maha Deepam day as part of Karthigai Deepam festival. When he returned home around 2 a.m., Siva opened the main entrance of the house and found cupboards in the living room and the bedroom door were broken. Police said that gold ornaments and cash kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was damaged to gain access to the house. Based on the alert, the Jolarpet police inspected the spot.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Police said sniffer dogs and fingerprint experts were roped. Footage from CCTV cameras in the house and on the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered and special teams were formed to nab the suspects. Further probe is under way.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Burglars decamp with 15 sovereigns of gold, cash from house near Jolarpet

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:34:03 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Burglars decamped with 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery, and around ₹1.2 lakh in cash from the house of a tribal family near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the victim as R. Siva, who belongs to the Irular community. He was living with his wife and son on the outskirts of the town. Siva went to Tiruvannamalai town for Maha Deepam day as part of Karthigai Deepam festival. When he returned home around 2 a.m., Siva opened the main entrance of the house and found cupboards in the living room and the bedroom door were broken. Police said that gold ornaments and cash kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was damaged to gain access to the house. Based on the alert, the Jolarpet police inspected the spot.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Police said sniffer dogs and fingerprint experts were roped. Footage from CCTV cameras in the house and on the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered and special teams were formed to nab the suspects. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:32:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepa' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha De' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha De' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai"?

B. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:09:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Right to choose a partner is an aspect of constitutional freedom, not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In his memorandum to Chairperson of Tamil Nadu Commission for the Prevention of Honour Killings, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder and Chidambaram MP, Thol. Thirumavalavan said, “the right to choose one’s partner is not a privilege granted by a family, caste or community” but “an aspect of the constitutional freedom and dignity of every individual”.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In his request to the Commission headed by Justice K.N. Basha, Mr. Thirumavalavan said that the Commission should “recommend the enactment of a comprehensive Tamil Nadu law against honour killings and honour-based crimes, with a broad definition rooted in the right to choose a partner and individual autonomy”. He further urged the Commission to provide a framework to address “collective and mob-based honour violence”, which would ensure that “every person who intentionally participates in, instigates, facilitates or enables the crime can be held accountable under clearly defined standards of criminal responsibility”. The VCK leader further said that enforceable duties and penalties should be imposed on police and public officials who fail to protect couples despite credible threats, including wilful refusal to register complaints, disclosure of confidential information and dereliction of preventive duties.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Thirumavalavan also demanded that there exist comprehensive protection for couples, survivors, witnesses and their families, including safehouses, relocation, legal aid, counselling, medical care, compensation and rehabilitation. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

3. He also appealed to the Commission to submit “a draft Bill and a time-bound implementation framework to the Government of Tamil Nadu, with budgetary allocations, monitoring arrangements and annual reporting to the Legislature”.

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. The protesters raised slogans alleging lack of safety for women. The DMK’s women wing also staged a demonstration at the Four Roads junction in Kallakurichi demanding the arrest of the MLA. They burnt the effigy of the MLA and raised slogans against him.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed in strength at the MLA’s office in Kallakurichi.

articles.title: No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say they have received no such communication and warn that Section 163 of BNSS remains in force in the area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls , scheduled for November 26 , senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration. The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands. An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu , was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.” The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added. “We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu . Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration. Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action. However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions. The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 01:17:28 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say they have received no such communication and warn that Section 163 of BNSS remains in force in the area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: No permission has been sought from the Delhi Police for a protest march against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls , scheduled for November 26 , senior New Delhi police officials said. The organisers, however, maintained that they had intimated the police about the proposed demonstration. The Delhi wing of the People Against SIR platform has called for a march on Constitution Day from Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg towards Jantar Mantar. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of SIR and the restoration of Jantar Mantar as a designated site for peaceful protests, among other demands. An email dated November 23, 2026, seen by The Hindu , was sent to the Delhi Police to inform them about the proposed programme. It stated: “This is to inform you that we, the Delhi People Against SIR, are going to observe Constitution Day as per the details given.” The email further stated that participants would assemble outside Valmiki Sadan on Mandir Marg at 12.30 p.m. on November 26 and march towards Jantar Mantar via Kali Bari Marg. “This is for your information and any follow-up/arrangements,” it added. “We make sure not to ask for permission but only inform the police about the march,” Maimoona Mollah, a representative of the platform, told The Hindu . Ms. Mollah claimed that the police had acknowledged the intimation and subsequently sought further details, including the proposed route and the expected number of participants expected. These details, she said, were shared with the police over a telephone conversation. The organisers have also announced plans to burn copies of the SIR notification during the demonstration. Public notice 🔶Information has been received that Samyukta Kisan Morcha and other activists are planning a protest march from Kali Bari to Jantar Mantar on 26.11.2026. No application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted for the said march. 🔶Section 163 BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi District. Unauthorised gatherings, processions, demonstrations, speeches, sloganeering and dharnas are prohibited. 🔶All are requested to comply with the order u/s 163 BNSS and cooperate with Police. Violations will invite legal action. However, New Delhi police officers denied receiving the intimation and stressed that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remain in force in the area and warned that action would be taken against gatherings in violation of the restrictions. The police said “preventive” security measures would be put in place to prevent any unauthorised gathering in the area. These would include multi-layer barricading, deployment of additional personnel and preventive detentions, if required, to disperse crowds and prevent protesters from assembling in violation of the prohibitory orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: People Against SIR was formed on October 14 following an emergency consultation in Delhi attended by representatives of more than 200 organisations. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18 States to campaign against the SIR exercise.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Permissibility (Noun)
कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।
✓ Syn: Admissibility, Legality, Allowance  |  ✖ Ant: Prohibition, Ban, Illegality
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Representative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Representative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Communication (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Communication' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR ma' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "People Against SIR emailed the police details of the proposed Constitution Day march from Valmiki Sadan to Jantar Mantar; the police, however, say..." (Hinglish Arth: पीपुल्स अगेंस्ट एसआईआर ने पुलिस को वाल्मिकी सदन से जंतर-मंतर तक प्रस्तावित संविधान दिवस मार्च का विवरण ईमेल किया; हालाँकि, पुलिस का कहना है कि उन्हें ऐसा कोई संचार नहीं मिला है और चेतावनी दी है कि बीएनएस की धारा 163)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "No permission sought for November 26 anti-SIR march, Delhi Police say; organisers say ‘intimation’ sent"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The national platform brings together 145 civil society groups, farmers’ unions, workers’ organisations, and women’s and youth groups across 18..." (Hinglish Arth: राष्ट्रीय मंच एसआईआर अभ्यास के खिलाफ अभियान चलाने के लिए 18 राज्यों के 145 नागरिक समाज समूहों, किसान संघों, श्रमिक संगठनों और महिलाओं और युवा समूहों को एक साथ लाता है।)

articles.title: Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided. Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders. “And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally. The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30. The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute. The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144. A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise. Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144. A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise. Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 02:48:50 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court indicated orally on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) its inclination to set aside a Calcutta High Court order that put on hold the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections over a delimitation exercise, and requested the High Court to hear the dispute afresh. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the suggestion while hearing an appeal filed by the West Bengal government against the High Court order of November 6. The High Court had directed the West Bengal State Election Commission to not notify the elections until a petition challenging the delimitation of municipal wards was decided. Chief Justice Kant said the apex court was inclined to set aside the order of the High Court after taking into consideration pertinent legal and factual issues raised by the State government. The writ petition could also be transferred from the Single Judge Bench to a Division Bench, which would consider the entire dispute afresh and pass appropriate orders. “And till the Division Bench forms a view the polls can be held off,” the court suggested orally. The lawyers for both the State and former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das, who had filed the petition in the High Court against the delimitation exercise, sought time to take instructions. The court listed the case for further hearing on November 30. The Bench reasoned that its proposed “ad-hoc arrangement” would place both parties on an “even keel” without the Supreme Court expressing any opinion on the merits of the dispute. The KMC had undertaken a revision of municipal ward boundaries ahead of the civic polls. As part of the plan, the number of wards in the civic body may rise to 209 from the current 144. A Division Bench of the High Court had stopped the State Election Commission from issuing the election notification till the Single Judge Bench hearing Mr. Das’s petition decided the legality of the ward delimitation exercise. Mr. Das had questioned the delimitation, arguing that the expansion of the municipal wards was void. He had sought a quashing of the September 11 gazette notification on expansion of wards as bad in law. He had contended that the delimitation happened on the basis of electoral rolls instead of the actual population, resulting in the alleged exclusion of a substantial number of residents.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: After the Single Judge Bench had refused his pleas for an interim stay of the elections, Mr. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.

Consideration (Noun)
सोच-विचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Consideration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Delimitation (Adjective / Verb)
परिसीमन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Delimitation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Notification (Noun)
अधिसूचना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Notification' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inclination (Adjective / Verb)
झुकाव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Inclination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitatio' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimita' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimita' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Supreme Court lists the case for hearing on November 30 after lawyers seek time to get instructions on the suggestion from the court." (Hinglish Arth: वकीलों द्वारा अदालत से सुझाव पर निर्देश प्राप्त करने के लिए समय मांगने के बाद सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने मामले को 30 नवंबर को सुनवाई के लिए सूचीबद्ध किया है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Supreme Court suggests referring KMC delimitation case back to High Court for fresh look"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Das had moved the High Court’s Division Bench." (Hinglish Arth: दास ने उच्च न्यायालय की खंडपीठ का रुख किया था।)

articles.title: Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”. Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon , but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 02:46:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”. Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon , but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign. During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security. He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution. “We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar. At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 01:53:32 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign. During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security. He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution. “We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar. At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district.

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।

✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Participation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Participation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inauguration (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Inauguration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign.

D. The author contends that 'Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth S' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "This was a promise made the BJP during their 2026 Assembly election campaign." (Hinglish Arth: यह एक वादा था जो भाजपा ने अपने 2026 के विधानसभा चुनाव अभियान के दौरान किया था)

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay said that the government was putting effort to follow own Indian culture and tradition and Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony. “We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya. “As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college. In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes. Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients. Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Uttariya instead of robes: West Bengal Government suggests universities to adopt Indian attire in convocations

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 04:01:27 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay said that the government was putting effort to follow own Indian culture and tradition and Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: West Bengal Higher Education Department has advised all the State-aided universities to adopt Indian attire such as Uttariya and clothes made of handloom fabric instead of Western robes during convocation or any academic ceremony. “We are putting effort to follow our own Indian culture and tradition. Uttariyo is enough for such ceremonies. Why do we have to wear robes? Many institutions, including the Indian Institute of Technology [IIT], have adopted only uttariya. Hence, we made the suggestion,” West Bengal Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay told media persons on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The development also came days after Mr. Chattopadhyay praised the Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College for upholding Indian traditions by replacing the conventional academic gown with a traditional uttariya. “As we strive to build a self-reliant Bharat, our education system must also reflect our civilisational values and cultural identity,” he wrote on X congratulating the students of the college. In its notice sent to all the vice chancellors of the universities, the department has now said that the UGC had not prescribed any rigid uniform design for ceremonial robes. Hence, the universities have the flexibility to incorporate traditional Indian attire, such as the uttariya, and to design distinct ceremonial attire for dignitaries and degree recipients. Monday’s (November 23) notice to the VCs said that the ceremonial attire made from Indian handloom was more suited to India’s climate. Such a preference for handloom fabrics and traditional Indian attire also supports the rural handloom industry and weavers’ livelihoods, it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “In view of the above, you are requested to take necessary steps to consider adopting handloom fabrics and traditional attire for the academic robes worn during convocation in your esteemed university as well as affiliated colleges, wherever applicable,” the department stated in the advisory asking the universities to send to confirmation of the communication to the department.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Civilisational (Adjective)
सभ्यतागत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Civilisational' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Communication (Noun)
संचार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Communication' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conventional (Adjective)
पारंपरिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conventional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
