Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking ASHA workers not to ‘blackmail’ government", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Rejecting their demand for a written assurance, the CM urged workers to end strike and resume duties.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking ASHA' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking A' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar tells striking A' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. (Hinglish Arth: लिखित आश्वासन की उनकी मांग को खारिज करते हुए सीएम ने कर्मचारियों से हड़ताल खत्म करने और काम पर लौटने का आग्रह किया।)

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Congress leader Manickam Tagore questions Udhayanidhi’s meeting with Tamil Nadu Governor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Tamil Nadu Congress chief recalls DMK leader’s earlier remarks describing the Governor as a ‘postman’ and raises doubts over DMK-BJP understanding.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president and Virudhunagar MP B. Manickam Tagore on Thursday (November 26, 2026) questioned Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin’s decision to meet Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and submit a petition, recalling his earlier remarks describing the Governor as a “postman.” Mr. Tagore asked how the DMK leader could now approach the same constitutional authority after having questioned his authority and made disparaging remarks about his office. Addressing mediapersons along with Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan and Tourism Minister S. Rajesh Kumar at Chennai, he also raised questions about whether there had been an “understanding” between the DMK and the BJP on the delimitation issue and whether the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) cases against DMK leaders had been settled. “Udhayanidhi and the DMK must first answer these questions,” he said. Responding to a question on the Congress’s own position on the Governor, given that its Ministers had approached him on matters concerning the appointment of Vice-Chancellors, Mr. Tagore said the Congress had never opposed the institution of the Governor. “The Congress believes that the Governor’s post should continue and that the person holding the office must act impartially and remain above politics. The Governor should provide accurate information to the Union government, work in coordination with the State government and not create unnecessary friction between the two,” he said. On the allegations concerning the Kallakurichi MLA and the complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer , Mr. Tagore said a fair investigation should be allowed to proceed and those found guilty should face action. He maintained that the safety of women, particularly those working in public institutions, was paramount. “If anyone has committed a mistake, it is the government’s duty to conduct a proper investigation and punish them. Women have struggled for generations to enter education and the workforce. Ensuring their safety is everyone’s responsibility. Those holding positions of responsibility must be doubly careful,” he said. National Commission for Women calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi MLA-Collector issue TVK faces criticism from Congress over law and order in Tamil Nadu, allegations against Kallakurichi MLA
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case, says Thirumavalavan

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Congress leader Manickam Tagore questions Udhayanidhi’s meeting with Tamil Nadu Governor

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 07:01:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Tamil Nadu Congress chief recalls DMK leader’s earlier remarks describing the Governor as a ‘postman’ and raises doubts over DMK-BJP understanding.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president and Virudhunagar MP B. Manickam Tagore on Thursday (November 26, 2026) questioned Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin’s decision to meet Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and submit a petition, recalling his earlier remarks describing the Governor as a “postman.” Mr. Tagore asked how the DMK leader could now approach the same constitutional authority after having questioned his authority and made disparaging remarks about his office. Addressing mediapersons along with Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan and Tourism Minister S. Rajesh Kumar at Chennai, he also raised questions about whether there had been an “understanding” between the DMK and the BJP on the delimitation issue and whether the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) cases against DMK leaders had been settled. “Udhayanidhi and the DMK must first answer these questions,” he said. Responding to a question on the Congress’s own position on the Governor, given that its Ministers had approached him on matters concerning the appointment of Vice-Chancellors, Mr. Tagore said the Congress had never opposed the institution of the Governor. “The Congress believes that the Governor’s post should continue and that the person holding the office must act impartially and remain above politics. The Governor should provide accurate information to the Union government, work in coordination with the State government and not create unnecessary friction between the two,” he said. On the allegations concerning the Kallakurichi MLA and the complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer , Mr. Tagore said a fair investigation should be allowed to proceed and those found guilty should face action. He maintained that the safety of women, particularly those working in public institutions, was paramount. “If anyone has committed a mistake, it is the government’s duty to conduct a proper investigation and punish them. Women have struggled for generations to enter education and the workforce. Ensuring their safety is everyone’s responsibility. Those holding positions of responsibility must be doubly careful,” he said. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case, says Thirumavalavan

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Responsibility (Noun)
ज़िम्मेदारी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Responsibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

A. The Tamil Nadu Congress chief recalls DMK leader’s earlier remarks describing the Governor as a ‘postman’ and raises doubts over DMK-BJP understanding.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Congress leader Manickam Tagore questions Udhaya' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Congress leader Manickam Tagore questions Udh' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Congress leader Manickam Tagore questions Udh' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Tamil Nadu Congress chief recalls DMK leader’s earlier remarks describing the Governor as a ‘postman’ and raises doubts over DMK-BJP understanding." A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case, says Thirumavalavan.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case, says Thirumavalavan." articles.title: Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Serbia 's Parliament speaker on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set an early Presidential election for December 27, after former President Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to pursue what turned out to be a failed bid to become Prime Minister. The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25. Mr. Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for Prime Minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as President, and was banned by law from seeking a third term. “I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programmes," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.” It was not immediately clear who the Presidential candidates will be. Mr. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election. The Presidency in Serbia is largely ceremonial. The President commands the Army and has a say in foreign policy but has no executive powers. While he was in office, however, Mr. Vucic concentrated power in the Presidency, facing accusations of authoritarian rule. Mr. Vucic regularly announced important state decisions and policies and even presided over government sessions. Since losing power, Mr. Vucic has accused the election winners of imposing a “revolutionary terror,” although his government is still technically in control until a new one is formed. The change in power has led to a surge in detentions of officials and police officers suspected of abusing their positions during Mr. Vucic's rule.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The youth-led movement had led two years of street protests that started in response to a train station canopy collapse in northern Serbia that killed 16 people. Many blamed the tragedy on alleged rampant corruption and negligence during the building renovation in Novi Sad.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Serbia sets Presidential election for December 27 after students won Parliamentary vote

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 07:25:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Serbia 's Parliament speaker on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set an early Presidential election for December 27, after former President Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to pursue what turned out to be a failed bid to become Prime Minister. The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25. Mr. Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for Prime Minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as President, and was banned by law from seeking a third term. “I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programmes," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.” It was not immediately clear who the Presidential candidates will be. Mr. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election. The Presidency in Serbia is largely ceremonial. The President commands the Army and has a say in foreign policy but has no executive powers. While he was in office, however, Mr. Vucic concentrated power in the Presidency, facing accusations of authoritarian rule. Mr. Vucic regularly announced important state decisions and policies and even presided over government sessions. Since losing power, Mr. Vucic has accused the election winners of imposing a “revolutionary terror,” although his government is still technically in control until a new one is formed. The change in power has led to a surge in detentions of officials and police officers suspected of abusing their positions during Mr. Vucic's rule.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The youth-led movement had led two years of street protests that started in response to a train station canopy collapse in northern Serbia that killed 16 people. Many blamed the tragedy on alleged rampant corruption and negligence during the building renovation in Novi Sad.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

प्रगतिशील — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Progressive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Parliament (Adjective)
संसद — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Parliament' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr.

The Presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Mr. Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early Parliamentary ballot on October 25. Mr. Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for Prime Minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as President, and was banned by law from seeking a third term. “I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programmes," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.” It was not immediately clear who the Presidential candidates will be. Mr. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election. The Presidency in Serbia is largely ceremonial. The President commands the Army and has a say in foreign policy but has no executive powers. While he was in office, however, Mr. Vucic concentrated power in the Presidency, facing accusations of authoritarian rule. Mr. Vucic regularly announced important state decisions and policies and even presided over government sessions. Since losing power, Mr. Vucic has accused the election winners of imposing a “revolutionary terror,” although his government is still technically in control until a new one is formed. The change in power has led to a surge in detentions of officials and police officers suspected of abusing their positions during Mr. Vucic's rule.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The youth-led movement had led two years of street protests that started in response to a train station canopy collapse in northern Serbia that killed 16 people. Many blamed the tragedy on alleged rampant corruption and negligence during the building renovation in Novi Sad.

articles.title: U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net migration to the U.K. has fallen to 77,000, its lowest levels since 1997, excluding the pandemic, as per official U.K. government figures released on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group immigrating and emigrating longterm to and from the U.K. The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 9,00,000 in the year ending June 2023. The news is likely to a shot in the arm for the governing Labour Party, as migration has become a political lighting-rod in recent years. The latest drop in numbers was predominantly due to a fall in non-EU migration to the U.K. This figure fell by more then 1,00,000 while emigration remained mostly stable. Non-EU+ nationals arriving in the U.K. fell by 17% to 7,38,000. Just under half came to study, a quarter for work, and 13% for asylum. Of those migrating to the U.K., the largest group consisted of Indians , then Chinese, then Nigerians, Pakistanis and Americans. Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed. More EU+ and British nationals left the U.K. than non-EU+ nationals. Some 2,45,00 Britons left the country longterm in the year ending June 2026, with net migration of Britons at -1,37,000.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These record high net migration numbers in 2023 — called the ‘Boriswave’, occurred during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative, following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, when visa rules were eased to fill certain occupations such as social care. Migration from non-EU countries consequently increased at this time. Mr. Johnson’s successors, Rishi Sunak, a fellow Conservative, and then Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the Labour Party, further tightened immigration policies resulting in falling numbers.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 U.K. net migration falls to lowest since 1997; Indians largest foreign group entering and leaving the country

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 06:25:21 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net migration to the U.K. has fallen to 77,000, its lowest levels since 1997, excluding the pandemic, as per official U.K. government figures released on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Indians constituted the largest foreign nationality group immigrating and emigrating longterm to and from the U.K. The net migration figure, which represents the number of people arriving in the U.K. minus those emigrating, fell dramatically from 2,04,000 for the year ending June 2025 and from a record high of 9,00,000 in the year ending June 2023. The news is likely to a shot in the arm for the governing Labour Party, as migration has become a political lighting-rod in recent years. The latest drop in numbers was predominantly due to a fall in non-EU migration to the U.K. This figure fell by more then 1,00,000 while emigration remained mostly stable. Non-EU+ nationals arriving in the U.K. fell by 17% to 7,38,000. Just under half came to study, a quarter for work, and 13% for asylum. Of those migrating to the U.K., the largest group consisted of Indians , then Chinese, then Nigerians, Pakistanis and Americans. Some 44,000 Indians arrived in the U.K. for work-related reasons, 77,000 to study, and 5,000 for other reasons. Some 28,000 Indians on work visas left the U.K. and 55,000 on study visas departed. More EU+ and British nationals left the U.K. than non-EU+ nationals. Some 2,45,00 Britons left the country longterm in the year ending June 2026, with net migration of Britons at -1,37,000.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: These record high net migration numbers in 2023 — called the ‘Boriswave’, occurred during the administration of Boris Johnson, a Conservative, following Brexit and the COVID-19 pandemic, when visa rules were eased to fill certain occupations such as social care. Migration from non-EU countries consequently increased at this time. Mr. Johnson’s successors, Rishi Sunak, a fellow Conservative, and then Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the Labour Party, further tightened immigration policies resulting in falling numbers.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Indian pharma company Hetero begins supply of generic twice-yearly HIV prevention injection in Africa
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as an additional HIV prevention option, based on clinical evidence showing high efficacy in preventing HIV infection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Hyderabad-based pharmaceutical company Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir, a long-acting drug for HIV prevention, to three African countries. The company plans to supply 300,000 vials initially to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe. Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months. Hetero is launching the generic drug under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic. The company expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027. These tablets form part of the PrEP regimen and will be supplied by the original manufacturer, Gilead Sciences, in the interim. The launch follows Gilead’s non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, allowing them to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 eligible countries. The licensing arrangement is intended to expand access to the drug in low- and middle-income countries. Hetero said its generic injectable formulation and oral initiation tablets had received an Expert Review Panel recommendation, allowing eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels while regulatory approval or WHO prequalification processes continue. In Zimbabwe, procurement is being supported through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The company plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African countries in early 2027 and expand availability across other countries covered by its licence, subject to national regulatory approvals and procurement arrangements. It also plans to introduce generic lenacapavir in India in the coming months, subject to regulatory clearance.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Indian pharma company Hetero begins supply of generic twice-yearly HIV prevention injection in Africa

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 06:31:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as an additional HIV prevention option, based on clinical evidence showing high efficacy in preventing HIV infection

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Hyderabad-based pharmaceutical company Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir, a long-acting drug for HIV prevention, to three African countries. The company plans to supply 300,000 vials initially to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe. Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months. Hetero is launching the generic drug under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic. The company expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027. These tablets form part of the PrEP regimen and will be supplied by the original manufacturer, Gilead Sciences, in the interim. The launch follows Gilead’s non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, allowing them to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 eligible countries. The licensing arrangement is intended to expand access to the drug in low- and middle-income countries. Hetero said its generic injectable formulation and oral initiation tablets had received an Expert Review Panel recommendation, allowing eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels while regulatory approval or WHO prequalification processes continue. In Zimbabwe, procurement is being supported through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The company plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African countries in early 2027 and expand availability across other countries covered by its licence, subject to national regulatory approvals and procurement arrangements. It also plans to introduce generic lenacapavir in India in the coming months, subject to regulatory clearance.

articles.title: BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Researchers at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have secured an Indian patent for a low-cost nutrient medium that could make large-scale cultivation of microalgae more affordable, opening possibilities for applications in renewable fuels, carbon capture and biotechnology.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The patented innovation, titled “Nutrient Medium Composition for Mass Cultivation of Microalgae” (Patent No. 603126), has been developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, K. Pranav Narayan of the Department of Biological Sciences and research scholar Sama Sanghamitra, as per a press release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Microalgae are microscopic organisms that use sunlight and carbon dioxide to produce biomass. They are considered a promising resource for wastewater treatment, carbon dioxide capture, biofertilisers, food and nutraceutical products, and the production of biodiesel and other bio-based fuels. However, the high cost of cultivation has limited their large-scale adoption. The BITS team developed an alternative nutrient formulation using locally available agricultural-grade fertilisers instead of expensive laboratory-grade chemicals. The formulation supplies key nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur required for microalgal growth while reducing the complexity and cost of preparing the cultivation medium. The macronutrients needed to prepare 100 litres of the new medium cost about ₹2.40, compared with around ₹43 for the conventional Bold’s Basal Medium (BBM). The cost is estimated to be around ₹4.50 per 100 litres, making it significantly cheaper than conventional alternatives. The formulation is also easy to prepare and can be supplied as a dry powder, which can be dissolved in water before use. The technology was tested in laboratory, non-sterile and outdoor cultivation conditions. The microalgae was also successfully cultivated in a 10,000-litre open pond using natural sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers are now in discussions with a potential industry partner, which has proposed a two-month evaluation of the formulation for carbon capture and biomass production applications. They are also seeking collaborations with companies in biofuel, algal biotechnology and carbon management sectors to explore commercialisation of the technology.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 BITS Pilani-Hyderabad researchers develop affordable way to grow microalgae

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 05:54:00 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Researchers at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus, have secured an Indian patent for a low-cost nutrient medium that could make large-scale cultivation of microalgae more affordable, opening possibilities for applications in renewable fuels, carbon capture and biotechnology.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The patented innovation, titled “Nutrient Medium Composition for Mass Cultivation of Microalgae” (Patent No. 603126), has been developed by Sandip S. Deshmukh of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, K. Pranav Narayan of the Department of Biological Sciences and research scholar Sama Sanghamitra, as per a press release issued on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Microalgae are microscopic organisms that use sunlight and carbon dioxide to produce biomass. They are considered a promising resource for wastewater treatment, carbon dioxide capture, biofertilisers, food and nutraceutical products, and the production of biodiesel and other bio-based fuels. However, the high cost of cultivation has limited their large-scale adoption. The BITS team developed an alternative nutrient formulation using locally available agricultural-grade fertilisers instead of expensive laboratory-grade chemicals. The formulation supplies key nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur required for microalgal growth while reducing the complexity and cost of preparing the cultivation medium. The macronutrients needed to prepare 100 litres of the new medium cost about ₹2.40, compared with around ₹43 for the conventional Bold’s Basal Medium (BBM). The cost is estimated to be around ₹4.50 per 100 litres, making it significantly cheaper than conventional alternatives. The formulation is also easy to prepare and can be supplied as a dry powder, which can be dissolved in water before use. The technology was tested in laboratory, non-sterile and outdoor cultivation conditions. The microalgae was also successfully cultivated in a 10,000-litre open pond using natural sunlight and atmospheric carbon dioxide.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Researchers are now in discussions with a potential industry partner, which has proposed a two-month evaluation of the formulation for carbon capture and biomass production applications. They are also seeking collaborations with companies in biofuel, algal biotechnology and carbon management sectors to explore commercialisation of the technology.

Agricultural (Adjective)
कृषि — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Agricultural' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Conventional (Adjective)
पारंपरिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conventional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Audit seeks clarification on 36 transactions worth ₹19 lakh in Agriculture Department
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Employees are saying there have been misappropriation of funds through private bank accounts, manipulation of recipient IDs and diversion of salary and subsidy payments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Agriculture Department in Kalaburagi has come under scrutiny following an audit requisition seeking explanations and supporting documents for 36 financial transactions amounting to approximately ₹19 lakh, amid allegations that employee salaries and payments under agricultural schemes were routed through a private bank account instead of the prescribed government treasury system. The Office of the Principal Accountant General (Audit-II) Department issued a requisition on October 23, 2026 to the Assistant Director of Agriculture, Kalaburagi, as part of a data-driven audit of establishment expenditure. The department has been asked to produce original vouchers, K2 challan sheets, payment records and other supporting documents relating to the transactions. The audit assumes significance in the wake of written complaints submitted by two employees to the Joint Director of Agriculture saying that their salaries were credited through an individual’s private savings account instead of the prescribed K2 government treasury mechanism. The complainants have reportedly submitted bank statement identifying the account from which the payments originated. In one instance, an employee who did not receive salaries for August 2024 and April 2026 was paid dues in October 2026 through the same private bank account. The delayed payments and the alleged use of an individual account have raised questions about the disbursement mechanism and the officials who authorised the transactions. More significantly, audit records reportedly show nearly nine salary transactions amounting to around ₹4.85 lakh between September and December 2025 in the name of an employee who has been on deputation to another department since 2022. In her complaint, the employee has questioned the purpose of these transactions and sought clarification on the account into which the salary amounts were credited.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: She has also stated that she is unaware of the transactions and the associated bank account details. She said that she was drawing her salary from the department to which she was deputed.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Kollam Additional Sessions Court has granted interim bail to Mohanan, the father-in-law of Vipanchika, who was found dead alongside her young daughter in Sharjah.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mohanan, who is currently abroad and listed as the third accused in the case, cannot be arrested until his anticipatory bail plea is formally considered by the court. The case was registered under charges of abetment to suicide, dowry harassment, and domestic violence. Reacting to the court’s decision, Vipanchika’s mother, Shailaja, demanded justice for her daughter and stated that allowing the accused to walk free amounts to a denial of justice. She also expressed suspicion that the accused are using high-level influence to manipulate the proceedings. Meanwhile, the first accused, Vipanchika’s husband Nidheesh, and the second accused, his sister Neethu, continue to remain abroad.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Vipanchika, 33, who worked as an HR manager at a private firm in Dubai, and her one-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Vaibhavi, were found dead in their Sharjah apartment on July 8, 2025. Investigations revealed that Vipanchika took her own life after killing her child. Prior to her death, a suicide note appeared on her Facebook page alleging continuous physical and mental torture over dowry by her husband and in-laws, alongside relentless pressure to agree to a divorce.

articles.title: Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electoral rolls too
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: TPCC flags at least three such instances in a single constituency (Bahadurpura)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Draft electoral rolls for graduate constituencies apparently have several duplicate entries despite the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s resolve to weed out the same. The rolls are prepared de-novo, which means that the existing rolls had been scrapped and voter details were sought afresh for inclusion. The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) has flagged at least three such instances in a single constituency of the city — Bahadurpura. In two of the three cases mentioned by the TPCC’s Election Cell, double registration on the voters’ part could be ruled out as even serial numbers and polling station number of the entries were the same. In the third case, details such as Electoral Photo Identity Card number, constituency name, polling station number and serial number, were missing. ECI has introduced a software as part of the ECINET app, to remove demographically and photo similar entries, as part of the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls. The software was apparently not run on the draft rolls for the MLC constituencies, because, in the three entries flagged, names, addresses and photos were the same, yet the duplicate entries had remained undiscovered. The TPCC has also urged Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudharshan Reddy to review the allocation of polling stations in the draft electoral roll for the forthcoming Graduates’ MLC elections, citing complaints that several voters have been assigned polling stations far from their residences. In a representation submitted on Thursday, P. Rajesh Kumar, chairman of the TPCC Election Commission Coordination Committee, said that several eligible graduates had been allotted polling stations located 10 to 14 km from their residential addresses, even though existing polling stations were available within 500 metres to one kilometre. He said such allocations were causing inconvenience to voters and could discourage them from exercising their franchise, particularly senior citizens, women and persons with disabilities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Rajesh Kumar urged the CEO to consider objections and representations received during the prescribed period for filing claims against the draft electoral roll and examine the feasibility of allotting polling stations closer to voters’ residences.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electoral rolls too

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 07:26:29 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: TPCC flags at least three such instances in a single constituency (Bahadurpura)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Draft electoral rolls for graduate constituencies apparently have several duplicate entries despite the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s resolve to weed out the same. The rolls are prepared de-novo, which means that the existing rolls had been scrapped and voter details were sought afresh for inclusion. The Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) has flagged at least three such instances in a single constituency of the city — Bahadurpura. In two of the three cases mentioned by the TPCC’s Election Cell, double registration on the voters’ part could be ruled out as even serial numbers and polling station number of the entries were the same. In the third case, details such as Electoral Photo Identity Card number, constituency name, polling station number and serial number, were missing. ECI has introduced a software as part of the ECINET app, to remove demographically and photo similar entries, as part of the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls. The software was apparently not run on the draft rolls for the MLC constituencies, because, in the three entries flagged, names, addresses and photos were the same, yet the duplicate entries had remained undiscovered. The TPCC has also urged Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudharshan Reddy to review the allocation of polling stations in the draft electoral roll for the forthcoming Graduates’ MLC elections, citing complaints that several voters have been assigned polling stations far from their residences. In a representation submitted on Thursday, P. Rajesh Kumar, chairman of the TPCC Election Commission Coordination Committee, said that several eligible graduates had been allotted polling stations located 10 to 14 km from their residential addresses, even though existing polling stations were available within 500 metres to one kilometre. He said such allocations were causing inconvenience to voters and could discourage them from exercising their franchise, particularly senior citizens, women and persons with disabilities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Rajesh Kumar urged the CEO to consider objections and representations received during the prescribed period for filing claims against the draft electoral roll and examine the feasibility of allotting polling stations closer to voters’ residences.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Inclusive (Adjective)
समावेशी — जिसमें समाज के हर वर्ग (खासकर गरीब और वंचित वर्ग) को बराबर शामिल किया जाए।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Egalitarian, All-encompassing  |  ✖ Ant: Exclusive, Discriminatory, Narrow
Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inconvenience (Adjective / Verb)
असुविधा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Inconvenience' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electoral rolls too", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. TPCC flags at least three such instances in a single constituency (Bahadurpura).
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electoral r' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electora' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electora' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "TPCC flags at least three such instances in a single constituency (Bahadurpura)." (Hinglish Arth: टीपीसीसी ने एक ही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र (बहादुरपुरा) में कम से कम तीन ऐसे उदाहरणों को चिह्नित किया)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Duplicate entries flagged in de-novo electoral rolls too"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Rajesh Kumar urged the CEO to consider objections and representations received during the prescribed period for filing claims against the draft...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Rajesh Kumar urged the CEO to consider objections and representations received during the prescribed period for filing claims against the draft..." (Hinglish Arth: राजेश कुमार ने सीईओ से मसौदा मतदाता सूची के खिलाफ दावे दायर करने के लिए निर्धारित अवधि के दौरान प्राप्त आपत्तियों और अभ्यावेदनों पर विचार करने और मतदान केंद्रों को आवंटित करने की व्यवहार्यता की जांच करने का आग्रह किया।)

articles.title: More migrant children in aided than in govt. schools in Keralam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in 2025-26 academic year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More migrant workers’ children study in aided schools than in government schools in Keralam, according to the General Education department. As many as 56.39% of the total migrant children in Classes I to X in the State in 2025-26 studied in aided schools as compared to 41.19% in government institutions. Only 2.43% of them studied in unaided schools. The total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in the 2025-26 academic year, as per a report of the Statistics wing at the Directorate of General Education. Of the total 25,893 students, 14,600 were enrolled in aided schools, 10,665 in government schools, and 628 in unaided schools. Of the total migrant students, 14,172 were boys and 11,721 girls. The total number of students in 2025-26 was 5.6% more than the 24,525 who were enrolled in 2024-25. This was less of an increase than the 15.14% increase from 2023-24 to 2024-25. Of the 25,893 students from outside Keralam, 25,409 were from other States and 484 from other countries. More than a quarter of them were studying in Ernakulam district (28.03%), while the least were in Wayanad (2.27%). Malappuram (2,600), Thrissur (2,286), and Kozhikode (2,181) also had a substantial number of migrant students. The 25,409 inter-State migrant children belonged to 33 States and Union Territories. The highest number was from Assam (4,192), followed by Bihar (4,128), West Bengal (4,033), Tamil Nadu (3,969), and Uttar Pradesh (3,230). In 2024-25, the number of inter-State migrant children was 24,189. Students from neighbouring Nepal (469) constituted a chunk of the 484 migrants from other countries studying in schools in the State. Bangladesh (8) and Sri Lanka (2) too had students in Keralam, while there was miniscule representation from the U.K., France, Canada, the Philippines, and Yemen. In 2024-25, the number of students from other countries came to 336. While 7,682 of the migrant students were from the general category, 1,401 were from the Scheduled Castes, 593 from the Scheduled Tribes, 15,637 in OBC, and 104 in OEC, and 476 in other categories.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The maximum number of migrant student enrolments was in Class I (4,407), progressively reducing with an increase in grades with Class X enrolments being only 1,036.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 More migrant children in aided than in govt. schools in Keralam

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 07:28:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in 2025-26 academic year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More migrant workers’ children study in aided schools than in government schools in Keralam, according to the General Education department. As many as 56.39% of the total migrant children in Classes I to X in the State in 2025-26 studied in aided schools as compared to 41.19% in government institutions. Only 2.43% of them studied in unaided schools. The total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in the 2025-26 academic year, as per a report of the Statistics wing at the Directorate of General Education. Of the total 25,893 students, 14,600 were enrolled in aided schools, 10,665 in government schools, and 628 in unaided schools. Of the total migrant students, 14,172 were boys and 11,721 girls. The total number of students in 2025-26 was 5.6% more than the 24,525 who were enrolled in 2024-25. This was less of an increase than the 15.14% increase from 2023-24 to 2024-25. Of the 25,893 students from outside Keralam, 25,409 were from other States and 484 from other countries. More than a quarter of them were studying in Ernakulam district (28.03%), while the least were in Wayanad (2.27%). Malappuram (2,600), Thrissur (2,286), and Kozhikode (2,181) also had a substantial number of migrant students. The 25,409 inter-State migrant children belonged to 33 States and Union Territories. The highest number was from Assam (4,192), followed by Bihar (4,128), West Bengal (4,033), Tamil Nadu (3,969), and Uttar Pradesh (3,230). In 2024-25, the number of inter-State migrant children was 24,189. Students from neighbouring Nepal (469) constituted a chunk of the 484 migrants from other countries studying in schools in the State. Bangladesh (8) and Sri Lanka (2) too had students in Keralam, while there was miniscule representation from the U.K., France, Canada, the Philippines, and Yemen. In 2024-25, the number of students from other countries came to 336. While 7,682 of the migrant students were from the general category, 1,401 were from the Scheduled Castes, 593 from the Scheduled Tribes, 15,637 in OBC, and 104 in OEC, and 476 in other categories.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The maximum number of migrant student enrolments was in Class I (4,407), progressively reducing with an increase in grades with Class X enrolments being only 1,036.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Representation (Noun)
प्रतिनिधित्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Substantial (Adjective)
संतोषजनक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Substantial' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "More migrant children in aided than in govt. schools in Keralam", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in 2025-26 academic year.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'More migrant children in aided than in govt. sch' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'More migrant children in aided than in govt. ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'More migrant children in aided than in govt. ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Total number of migrant children in Classes I to X across government, aided, and unaided sectors crossed 25,000 in 2025-26 academic year." (Hinglish Arth: शैक्षणिक वर्ष 2025-26 में सरकारी, सहायता प्राप्त और गैर-सहायता प्राप्त क्षेत्रों में कक्षा I से X तक प्रवासी बच्चों की कुल संख्या 25,000 को पार कर गई)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "More migrant children in aided than in govt. schools in Keralam"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The maximum number of migrant student enrolments was in Class I (4,407), progressively reducing with an increase in grades with Class X enrolments...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The maximum number of migrant student enrolments was in Class I (4,407), progressively reducing with an increase in grades with Class X enrolments..." (Hinglish Arth: प्रवासी छात्रों के नामांकन की अधिकतम संख्या कक्षा I (4,407) में थी, जो धीरे-धीरे ग्रेड में वृद्धि के साथ कम हो रही थी और कक्षा X में नामांकन केवल 1,036 था।)

articles.title: BJP national office-bearers to meet from Friday; PM Modi likely to attend
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Two-day meeting at Pusa campus, to be chaired by party chief Nitin Nabin, is expected to deliberate on organisational matters ahead of 2027 Assembly elections

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national office-bearers are expected to deliberate on a wide range of organisational matters at a two-day meeting beginning Friday (November 27, 2026), against the backdrop of the 2027 Assembly elections in several States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is also likely to attend the meeting, which will be presided over by BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the Pusa campus in Delhi. The Prime Minister had earlier interacted with the party’s newly appointed national office-bearers at the BJP headquarters on August 22, following their first formal meeting. On August 17, Mr. Nabin had announced his national organisational team, bringing in new faces and retaining several existing office-bearers. Former Union Minister Smriti Irani returned as general secretary, while former party general secretary Ram Madhav was appointed vice-president. Former Tripura Chief Minister Biplab Deb and Rajya Sabha MP Satish Poonia were also appointed general secretaries. Union Minister Piyush Goyal was appointed national treasurer. B.L. Santosh was retained as general secretary (organisation), with Shiv Prakash and Saudan Singh as joint general secretaries (organisation), while Uttarakhand MP Anil Baluni was retained as national media convenor. Only two general secretaries from the previous team, Sunil Bansal and Vinod Tawde, were also retained. Of the over 60 office-bearers, six are below 40 years of age, 15 are between 40 and 49, and 21 are between 50 and 59. The team includes 12 women, six of them vice-presidents.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bharatiya Janata Party / politics / state politics / politics (general) / national politics

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 BJP national office-bearers to meet from Friday; PM Modi likely to attend

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 07:24:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Two-day meeting at Pusa campus, to be chaired by party chief Nitin Nabin, is expected to deliberate on organisational matters ahead of 2027 Assembly elections

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national office-bearers are expected to deliberate on a wide range of organisational matters at a two-day meeting beginning Friday (November 27, 2026), against the backdrop of the 2027 Assembly elections in several States. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is also likely to attend the meeting, which will be presided over by BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the Pusa campus in Delhi. The Prime Minister had earlier interacted with the party’s newly appointed national office-bearers at the BJP headquarters on August 22, following their first formal meeting. On August 17, Mr. Nabin had announced his national organisational team, bringing in new faces and retaining several existing office-bearers. Former Union Minister Smriti Irani returned as general secretary, while former party general secretary Ram Madhav was appointed vice-president. Former Tripura Chief Minister Biplab Deb and Rajya Sabha MP Satish Poonia were also appointed general secretaries. Union Minister Piyush Goyal was appointed national treasurer. B.L. Santosh was retained as general secretary (organisation), with Shiv Prakash and Saudan Singh as joint general secretaries (organisation), while Uttarakhand MP Anil Baluni was retained as national media convenor. Only two general secretaries from the previous team, Sunil Bansal and Vinod Tawde, were also retained. Of the over 60 office-bearers, six are below 40 years of age, 15 are between 40 and 49, and 21 are between 50 and 59. The team includes 12 women, six of them vice-presidents.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Bharatiya Janata Party / politics / state politics / politics (general) / national politics

articles.title: Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 08:05:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient. The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL. Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment. “Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune. He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions. The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes. Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Supplementation (Noun)
अनुपूरण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Supplementation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Developmental (Adjective)
विकास संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Developmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Physiological (Adjective)
शारीरिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Physiological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

A. Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents,...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'Two-thirds of adolescents in India are defici' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents,..." A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme." 🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Cyclists take the green message through Attappady

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:28:23 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Pedal Force bicycle group organised a two-day 160-km cycling expedition to promote nature conservation. The ‘save planet cycle ride’ began from Kanjikode on November 22, 2026, passed through Anakkatti to Attappady, and returned to the starting point.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Organisers said the cycle ride aimed at spreading awareness of the need to protect the environment and encourage people to take an active role in conserving nature.

articles.title: Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Prakasam and Nellore districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The first phase of the Gram Panchaya elections were conduced peacefully across Markapuram, Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly 1.20 lakh voters out of the total 1.47 lakh exercised their right to vote during elections across 90 Gram Panchayats in six mandals of Markapuram district with a turnout of 81.70%. About 80.27% voter turnout was recorded with 1.55 lakh people among the total 1.93 lakh voters exercised their franchise during the elections across 81 Gram Panchayats in eight mandals of Prakasam district. While the notification has been issued for conducting elections in 139 panchayats, candidates were elected unanimously in 62 panchayats. Similarly, 782 ward members have been elected unopposed. In Kandukuru Municipality, 76.07% voter turnout was recorded during the polling for its 40 wards. Out of the 47,473 voters, 36,114 people exercise their franchise in the elections. In Kavali division of SPSR Nellore district, the first phase elections were scheduled for 134 Gram Panchayats. Of these, 17 Panchayats were elected unanimous, while polling took place in 117 Panchayats. Among these 117 in eight mandals of the district, Sarpanches were elected unanimously in three Panchayats. Over 1.93 lakh out of total 2.39 lakh voters across 114 Panchayats with a turnout of 80.60%. Gudur and Kavali Municipalities have witnessed voter turnout of 56.40% and 68.92% respectively. Out of total 80,492 voters in Gudur, 45,400 polled, while 58,884 polled among the overall 85,433 voters in Kavali. Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said that the polling concluded peacefully. “The public showed great interest in the Sarpanch elections, with a higher participation rate compared to general elections,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He personally visited Sunnambatti in Dagadarthi mandal, as well as Viswanatharaopeta and KK Gunta villages in Bogolu mandal, to inspect the polling process. He inquired about the poll management process.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Prakasam and Nellore districts

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 09:24:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The first phase of the Gram Panchaya elections were conduced peacefully across Markapuram, Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nearly 1.20 lakh voters out of the total 1.47 lakh exercised their right to vote during elections across 90 Gram Panchayats in six mandals of Markapuram district with a turnout of 81.70%. About 80.27% voter turnout was recorded with 1.55 lakh people among the total 1.93 lakh voters exercised their franchise during the elections across 81 Gram Panchayats in eight mandals of Prakasam district. While the notification has been issued for conducting elections in 139 panchayats, candidates were elected unanimously in 62 panchayats. Similarly, 782 ward members have been elected unopposed. In Kandukuru Municipality, 76.07% voter turnout was recorded during the polling for its 40 wards. Out of the 47,473 voters, 36,114 people exercise their franchise in the elections. In Kavali division of SPSR Nellore district, the first phase elections were scheduled for 134 Gram Panchayats. Of these, 17 Panchayats were elected unanimous, while polling took place in 117 Panchayats. Among these 117 in eight mandals of the district, Sarpanches were elected unanimously in three Panchayats. Over 1.93 lakh out of total 2.39 lakh voters across 114 Panchayats with a turnout of 80.60%. Gudur and Kavali Municipalities have witnessed voter turnout of 56.40% and 68.92% respectively. Out of total 80,492 voters in Gudur, 45,400 polled, while 58,884 polled among the overall 85,433 voters in Kavali. Nellore Collector Himanshu Shukla said that the polling concluded peacefully. “The public showed great interest in the Sarpanch elections, with a higher participation rate compared to general elections,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He personally visited Sunnambatti in Dagadarthi mandal, as well as Viswanatharaopeta and KK Gunta villages in Bogolu mandal, to inspect the polling process. He inquired about the poll management process.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Municipality (Noun)
नगर पालिका — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Municipality' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Management (Adjective)
प्रबंध — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Management' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Prakasam and Nellore districts", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The first phase of the Gram Panchaya elections were conduced peacefully across Markapuram, Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts on Thursday.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Prakasam' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Praka' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Praka' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The first phase of the Gram Panchaya elections were conduced peacefully across Markapuram, Prakasam and SPSR Nellore districts on Thursday." (Hinglish Arth: ग्राम पंचाय चुनाव का पहला चरण गुरुवार को मार्कापुरम, प्रकाशम और एसपीएसआर नेल्लोर जिलों में शांतिपूर्ण ढंग से संपन्न हुआ।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Panchayat polls peaceful in Markapuram, Prakasam and Nellore districts"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He inquired about the poll management process.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "He inquired about the poll management process." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने मतदान प्रबंधन प्रक्रिया की जानकारी ली.)
