articles.title: Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Sthanika Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day. The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules. A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said. Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police. An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They reasoned that the Utchipillaiyar Temple, the Rajagopuram, and the venue for burning chokkapanai near the 16-Pillar Mandapam lie on a straight line, and the Utchipillaiyar Temple was located right above the sanctum sanctorum. They also confirmed that they had given the same opinion “in writing” on November 7, 2013 and December 4, 2025. “The deepam is lit at the deepamandapam after getting oral or written opinion from us every year. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:30:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Sthanika Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day. The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules. A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said. Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police. An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They reasoned that the Utchipillaiyar Temple, the Rajagopuram, and the venue for burning chokkapanai near the 16-Pillar Mandapam lie on a straight line, and the Utchipillaiyar Temple was located right above the sanctum sanctorum. They also confirmed that they had given the same opinion “in writing” on November 7, 2013 and December 4, 2025. “The deepam is lit at the deepamandapam after getting oral or written opinion from us every year. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.

Administration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Traditional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Cooperation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Ceremonial (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Ceremonial' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statemen' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statemen' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa..."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Sthanika Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified."

articles.title: GVMC receives 803 applications during three days tax melas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A total of 803 applications were received during the three-day Revenue Tax Melas organised by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) across its zones from November 24 to 26, Commissioner Ketan Garg said on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The civic body received 93 applications on the first day, 394 on the second and 316 on the third. Among the zones, the North Zone recorded the highest number of submissions at 159, followed by Madhurawada 103 and East Zone with 97. Aganampudi recorded the lowest, at 27. According to Mr. Garg, requests for change of ownership accounted for the largest share with 229 applications, followed by 168 general revision petitions and 142 applications for new assessments. The corporation also received 87 applications for correction of house numbers, 38 for correction of owners’ names and 94 concerning other issues. The remaining applications were related to demolitions, assessment modifications, bifurcations, property tax exemptions and mergers.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Garg directed officials to scrutinise all applications and resolve the grievances promptly.

According to Mr. Garg, requests for change of ownership accounted for the largest share with 229 applications, followed by 168 general revision petitions and 142 applications for new assessments. The corporation also received 87 applications for correction of house numbers, 38 for correction of owners’ names and 94 concerning other issues. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Garg directed officials to scrutinise all applications and resolve the grievances promptly.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 GVMC receives 803 applications during three days tax melas

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:29:04 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A total of 803 applications were received during the three-day Revenue Tax Melas organised by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) across its zones from November 24 to 26, Commissioner Ketan Garg said on Thursday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The civic body received 93 applications on the first day, 394 on the second and 316 on the third. Among the zones, the North Zone recorded the highest number of submissions at 159, followed by Madhurawada 103 and East Zone with 97. Aganampudi recorded the lowest, at 27. According to Mr. Garg, requests for change of ownership accounted for the largest share with 229 applications, followed by 168 general revision petitions and 142 applications for new assessments. The corporation also received 87 applications for correction of house numbers, 38 for correction of owners’ names and 94 concerning other issues. The remaining applications were related to demolitions, assessment modifications, bifurcations, property tax exemptions and mergers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Garg directed officials to scrutinise all applications and resolve the grievances promptly.

A. A total of 803 applications were received during the three-day Revenue Tax Melas organised by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC)...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'GVMC receives 803 applications during three days' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'GVMC receives 803 applications during three d' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'GVMC receives 803 applications during three d' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A total of 803 applications were received during the three-day Revenue Tax Melas organised by the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC)..."

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Karnataka’s Escoms plan to pass profits to consumers via lower power bills from April 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In a relief for electricity consumers amid rising household expenses, electricity supply companies (Escoms) across Karnataka are likely to pass on their profits to consumers in the form of a refund of around 16 paise per unit from April 2027.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Sources in the Energy Department said on Thursday that most Escoms, including Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (Bescom), Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company (Gescom), Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC), and Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (Mescom), have recorded profits for the financial year 2025-26. However, Hubli Electricity Supply Company (Hescom) is an exception. A senior Energy Department official said the improved financial performance would enable Escoms to return the gains to consumers. Bescom alone reported a profit of ₹293.62 crore during 2025-26, while the profit figures of other Escoms are yet to be officially announced. Every year, Escoms are required to submit their tariff status and profit-and-loss statements, known as truing-up petitions, to the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) as part of their annual performance review. The companies are scheduled to submit their petitions on November 30. Once the proposals receive KERC’s approval, the refund will be adjusted against electricity bills for consumption from April 2027. While the average refund is expected to be around 16 paise per unit, consumers in some Escom jurisdictions could receive a higher benefit. Bescom sources said the company was seeking a refund of 35 paise per unit, although the proposal is yet to be finalised. The approved amount is expected to be announced on the Bescom website in December 2026.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Officials attributed the improved financial performance to a reduction in power distribution losses from 11% to around 9.13%. Escoms also reduced power procurement costs by utilising more electricity generated through hydropower instead of relying on relatively expensive thermal power.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Karnataka’s Escoms plan to pass profits to consumers via lower power bills from April 2027

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:25:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In a relief for electricity consumers amid rising household expenses, electricity supply companies (Escoms) across Karnataka are likely to pass on their profits to consumers in the form of a refund of around 16 paise per unit from April 2027.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Sources in the Energy Department said on Thursday that most Escoms, including Bangalore Electricity Supply Company (Bescom), Gulbarga Electricity Supply Company (Gescom), Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC), and Mangalore Electricity Supply Company (Mescom), have recorded profits for the financial year 2025-26. However, Hubli Electricity Supply Company (Hescom) is an exception. A senior Energy Department official said the improved financial performance would enable Escoms to return the gains to consumers. Bescom alone reported a profit of ₹293.62 crore during 2025-26, while the profit figures of other Escoms are yet to be officially announced. Every year, Escoms are required to submit their tariff status and profit-and-loss statements, known as truing-up petitions, to the Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) as part of their annual performance review. The companies are scheduled to submit their petitions on November 30. Once the proposals receive KERC’s approval, the refund will be adjusted against electricity bills for consumption from April 2027. While the average refund is expected to be around 16 paise per unit, consumers in some Escom jurisdictions could receive a higher benefit. Bescom sources said the company was seeking a refund of 35 paise per unit, although the proposal is yet to be finalised. The approved amount is expected to be announced on the Bescom website in December 2026.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Officials attributed the improved financial performance to a reduction in power distribution losses from 11% to around 9.13%. Escoms also reduced power procurement costs by utilising more electricity generated through hydropower instead of relying on relatively expensive thermal power.

articles.title: Workers of BJP, JD(S) stage protest opposing Operation Gaja at Kadabagere in Chikkamagaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Workers of the BJP and the JD(S) from Khandya hobli in Chikkamagaluru taluk jointly staged a protest at Kadabagere village on Thursday against Operation Gaja, the drive to push wild elephants from parts of Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The workers took out a protest march in the village and raised slogans against the State government and the Congress MLAs, alleging that they had failed to represent the farmers affected by the government’s decision. They described the operation, which seeks to drive the elephants to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, most of which lies in Chikkamagaluru district, as an unscientific move. Former Minister D.N. Jeevaraj said the Forest Department should take responsibility for the crisis. “The plantations we have cultivated have become more comfortable habitats for elephants than the actual forest. The forest consists mostly of trees like acacia, which contribute little to its biodiversity. Hence, elephants find our plantations more suitable,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also criticised the announcement by the Congress MLAs that they would resign, saying the legislators were only staging a drama instead of pressing the State government to protect the people of Chikkamagaluru from the elephant menace.

📰 Workers of BJP, JD(S) stage protest opposing Operation Gaja at Kadabagere in Chikkamagaluru

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:23:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Workers of the BJP and the JD(S) from Khandya hobli in Chikkamagaluru taluk jointly staged a protest at Kadabagere village on Thursday against Operation Gaja, the drive to push wild elephants from parts of Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The workers took out a protest march in the village and raised slogans against the State government and the Congress MLAs, alleging that they had failed to represent the farmers affected by the government’s decision. They described the operation, which seeks to drive the elephants to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, most of which lies in Chikkamagaluru district, as an unscientific move. Former Minister D.N. Jeevaraj said the Forest Department should take responsibility for the crisis. “The plantations we have cultivated have become more comfortable habitats for elephants than the actual forest. The forest consists mostly of trees like acacia, which contribute little to its biodiversity. Hence, elephants find our plantations more suitable,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He also criticised the announcement by the Congress MLAs that they would resign, saying the legislators were only staging a drama instead of pressing the State government to protect the people of Chikkamagaluru from the elephant menace.

articles.title: Four-member gang targeting cab, bike taxi drivers arrested in Bengaluru

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Gang allegedly committed over 30 robberies in three months to fund drug purchases; police trace 11 cases

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Whitefield police have busted an extortion racket and arrested four men who allegedly targeted cab and bike taxi drivers at night, assaulted them, and extorted money. The gang is suspected of having committed over two dozen such robberies in the past three months to fund their drug addiction and other vices. The accused have been identified as Manoj, Preetham Prakash, Syed Shafi, and Akhilesh, residents of Gandhipura and Vijayanagar in Whitefield. The arrests followed a complaint by Mohammed Nisar, a bike rider, who was allegedly intercepted and assaulted by the accused on an isolated stretch near Nallurhalli Metro station. The accused, who arrived in a car, allegedly assaulted him and forced him to transfer money online from his mobile phone before fleeing. Following the complaint, a team of Whitefield police, led by DCP Haribabu, launched an operation to track down the gang. The police traced the rental aggregator through which the accused had hired the car and followed the vehicle for around 2 km to 3 km. As the accused allegedly drove at high speed to evade the police, the investigators sought the rental company’s assistance in remotely switching off the car’s engine. When the vehicle came to a halt, the accused stepped out to check the engine. Police personnel surrounded the car and arrested three of them on the spot. The fourth accused, who initially managed to escape, was arrested later. The probe revealed that all four accused were drug users and allegedly committed the robberies to raise money to buy narcotics. The money extorted from drivers was reportedly transferred directly to the bank account of a suspected drug peddler. Manoj, the prime accused, allegedly planned the robberies and identified potential targets. Preetham Prakash, a BCom graduate, was his associate, while Syed Shafi worked as a cab driver and Akhilesh was employed as a tattoo artist. The gang initially used an autorickshaw to commit the robberies but later switched to a rented car to target drivers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: During interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed to committing around 30 robberies in three months. The police have so far traced and linked the gang to 11 incidents.

The accused have been identified as Manoj, Preetham Prakash, Syed Shafi, and Akhilesh, residents of Gandhipura and Vijayanagar in Whitefield. The arrests followed a complaint by Mohammed Nisar, a bike rider, who was allegedly intercepted and assaulted by the accused on an isolated stretch near Nallurhalli Metro station. The accused, who arrived in a car, allegedly assaulted him and forced him to transfer money online from his mobile phone before fleeing. Following the complaint, a team of Whitefield police, led by DCP Haribabu, launched an operation to track down the gang. The police traced the rental aggregator through which the accused had hired the car and followed the vehicle for around 2 km to 3 km. As the accused allegedly drove at high speed to evade the police, the investigators sought the rental company’s assistance in remotely switching off the car’s engine. When the vehicle came to a halt, the accused stepped out to check the engine. Police personnel surrounded the car and arrested three of them on the spot. The fourth accused, who initially managed to escape, was arrested later. The probe revealed that all four accused were drug users and allegedly committed the robberies to raise money to buy narcotics. The money extorted from drivers was reportedly transferred directly to the bank account of a suspected drug peddler. Manoj, the prime accused, allegedly planned the robberies and identified potential targets. Preetham Prakash, a BCom graduate, was his associate, while Syed Shafi worked as a cab driver and Akhilesh was employed as a tattoo artist. The gang initially used an autorickshaw to commit the robberies but later switched to a rented car to target drivers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: During interrogation, the accused allegedly confessed to committing around 30 robberies in three months. The police have so far traced and linked the gang to 11 incidents.

articles.title: CPI announces three-day ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ from December 1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Demands include CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, implementation of women’s quota, and legal MSP guarantee for farmers

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D. Raja on Thursday (November 26, 2026) announced a three-day “Jail Bharo Andolan” from December 1 to 3 on a set of political and economic demands, including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, implementation of women’s reservation, and a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Raja said the country was facing multiple crises, claiming that the economy was in a poor state, prices were rising and unemployment remained high. He also expressed concern over “increasing atrocities against minorities, Dalits, women and children.” The CPI leader said Prime Minister Narendra Modi often spoke and wrote about the Constitution but he should be “truthful to the people and the country”. He said the Constitution made it clear that India should remain a secular democratic republic and noted that B.R. Ambedkar had rejected the idea of a theocratic state. Mr. Raja accused Mr. Modi of seeking to establish a “Hindu Rashtra”, which he described as a “unidimensional, monolithic neoliberal medieval social order” that perpetuated caste inequalities and subverted the Constitution. Mr. Raja appealed to “all secular democratic forces” to unite against the BJP and work towards defeating the ruling party in the coming Assembly elections in five States.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He said the CPI had held informal discussions with the Samajwadi Party and the Congress regarding seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D. Raja on Thursday (November 26, 2026) announced a three-day “Jail Bharo Andolan” from December 1 to 3 on a set of political and economic demands, including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, implementation of women’s reservation, and a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers. Addressing a press conference, Mr. Raja said the country was facing multiple crises, claiming that the economy was in a poor state, prices were rising and unemployment remained high. He also expressed concern over “increasing atrocities against minorities, Dalits, women and children.” The CPI leader said Prime Minister Narendra Modi often spoke and wrote about the Constitution but he should be “truthful to the people and the country”. He said the Constitution made it clear that India should remain a secular democratic republic and noted that B.R. Ambedkar had rejected the idea of a theocratic state. Mr. Raja accused Mr. Modi of seeking to establish a “Hindu Rashtra”, which he described as a “unidimensional, monolithic neoliberal medieval social order” that perpetuated caste inequalities and subverted the Constitution. Mr. Raja appealed to “all secular democratic forces” to unite against the BJP and work towards defeating the ruling party in the coming Assembly elections in five States.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He said the CPI had held informal discussions with the Samajwadi Party and the Congress regarding seat-sharing in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territory held by the Iran-backed group including the capital Sanaa on Thursday (November 26, 2026), hours after it struck Riyadh. The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago. The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said during the night that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh, where residents and an AFP journalist heard an explosion. It also said it had destroyed a cruise missile launched towards the west of the country and a drone in the Jeddah region on the Red Sea. "The air force of the Saudi enemy today launched a series of strikes at the capital Sanaa," the Houthis' press agency reported on Thursday morning. An AFP journalist in Sanaa reported seeing smoke in the area of the airport. The Houthi news outlet Almasirah reported that the strikes targeted a factory and warehouses in Bani al-Harith. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), residents of the key Houthi-controlled port of Hodeida told AFP they had heard jets flying over the city and loud explosions. Almasirah said the strikes destroyed a wastewater treatment facility serving a densely populated district. The Houthis said the day before they had struck two Saudi ports on the Red Sea, after Saudi strikes on Hodeida.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.

📰 Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:09:34 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Houthi media reported a series of Saudi airstrikes against territory held by the Iran-backed group including the capital Sanaa on Thursday (November 26, 2026), hours after it struck Riyadh. The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago. The coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said during the night that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh, where residents and an AFP journalist heard an explosion. It also said it had destroyed a cruise missile launched towards the west of the country and a drone in the Jeddah region on the Red Sea. "The air force of the Saudi enemy today launched a series of strikes at the capital Sanaa," the Houthis' press agency reported on Thursday morning. An AFP journalist in Sanaa reported seeing smoke in the area of the airport. The Houthi news outlet Almasirah reported that the strikes targeted a factory and warehouses in Bani al-Harith. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), residents of the key Houthi-controlled port of Hodeida told AFP they had heard jets flying over the city and loud explosions. Almasirah said the strikes destroyed a wastewater treatment facility serving a densely populated district. The Houthis said the day before they had struck two Saudi ports on the Red Sea, after Saudi strikes on Hodeida.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group t' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group t' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war." (Hinglish Arth: यमन में पुनर्जीवित गृह युद्ध के दौरान हौथिस और सऊदी नेतृत्व वाले गठबंधन के बीच आदान-प्रदान लगभग दैनिक हो गया है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Yemen's Houthi-held capital hit after group targets Riyadh"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The coalition, meanwhile, said it had brought down a Houthi projectile targeting Jazan that had caused light damage and no civilian casualties." (Hinglish Arth: इस बीच, गठबंधन ने कहा कि उसने जाज़ान को निशाना बनाते हुए एक हौथी प्रोजेक्टाइल को मार गिराया, जिससे हल्की क्षति हुई और कोई नागरिक हताहत नहीं हुआ।)

articles.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy Education Minister, officials say
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Israeli airstrikes ‌and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, medics said, including the ​Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education in the Gaza Strip, in ⁠a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire. Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month. "No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu. The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role. Two other separate ​airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ⁠medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military didn't immediately comment on those seven reported deaths. Israel has continued to ‌carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament. Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed ‌since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Israel kills nine in Gaza, including Hamas-appointed deputy Education Minister, officials say

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 11:05:25 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the Deputy Gaza Education Minister, and his wife.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Israeli airstrikes ‌and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians overnight, medics said, including the ​Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education in the Gaza Strip, in ⁠a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-old ceasefire. Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month. "No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu. The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role. Two other separate ​airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ⁠medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military didn't immediately comment on those seven reported deaths. Israel has continued to ‌carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament. Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed ‌since the ceasefire was agreed in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya. The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures. The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it. "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media. Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate. The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated. Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution. The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution. Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Myanmar has maintained that operations undertaken by its security forces in northern Rakhine state during 2016–2018 ⁠were counter-terrorism actions against an insurgent group.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya. The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it. "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media. Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate. The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated. Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution. The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution. Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The government must build consensus on delimitation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appears to have zeroed in on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies as the central piece of its strategy for the next general election, due in 2029. As the current constitutional scheme stands, a fresh delimitation is triggered once the data from the ongoing Census 2027 is published . That default path, which is based on population distribution across States, will considerably cut down the representation of States that have stabilised their population since the last delimitation. The Centre has now proposed to extend the constitutional freeze on inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, while increasing the size of the House to a maximum of 850 seats. The demarcation of the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies will be based on the 2011 Census within each State. The delimitation exercise will also bring into force 33% reservation for women , which Parliament approved in 2023. Considering the need to balance the ‘one person, one vote’ principle with the principles of federalism, which is about protecting the group rights of States, the proposals are a reasonable way forward for India. That said, the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats is such a central question of democracy and federalism that any changes must be preceded by thoughtful deliberations at multiple levels. That makes the approach of the Centre , which is trying to pass a constitutional amendment through defections and manipulations, dubious and lacking in good faith. If the Centre has been willing to extend the constitutional guarantee of inter-State distribution of seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, it could have built an all-party consensus on the issue . Instead, in April, it made a deceptive move by promising to maintain the current proportion of seats while the constitutional amendment it moved would have made that promise unconstitutional. At present, when the Centre is keen to appear accommodative, a more appropriate manner to proceed with such a generational measure in India’s federal democracy is to refer the Bills to a parliamentary committee that can examine them in detail and generate a national conversation. A bigger Lok Sabha will create its own challenges , while the case for increasing its size is not entirely without merit as India’s population has grown by at least 2.6 times since the 1971 Census, which forms the basis of the last delimitation of 1973, based on the 1971 Census. 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The economic and diplomatic consequences of India’s efforts to estrange Pakistan often overshadow the costs distributed between them. For example, Pakistani space scientists can today access facilities in China whereas Indian space scientists can access facilities in the United States and Europe . But Indian scientists studying environmental conditions in Pakistan and Pakistani scientists studying conditions in India have far fewer alternatives. The latter matters much more for regional development and stability. On November 25, Beijing’s ‘Space Silk Road’ diplomacy and the strain on New Delhi’s hedging strategies converged in the Shenzhou-24 mission as China launched Pakistan’s first astronaut , Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, to the Tiangong space station. Pakistan had offered in 2015 to contribute to India’s proposed SAARC satellite and wanted the project administered under SAARC, but India insisted on operating it as largesse to its neighbours. If it had really been SAARC’s satellite, ISRO and its Pakistani counterpart, SUPARCO , could have developed an institutional relationship and India could have influenced its neighbour’s space programme through a multilateral mechanism. But today, India’s ability to engage Pakistan on regional matters has increasingly depended on negotiating with powers beyond South Asia, in institutions with other agendas. Even as spaceflight emerges as a new geopolitical realm, its substantial scientific component affords countries opportunities to engage independently of interstate relations in other domains. The Shenzhou-24 experience will be significant for SUPARCO just as the Axiom-4 mission in the U.S. was for ISRO , helping to significantly lower Islamabad’s cost to access similar future opportunities, especially those under the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organization, which also includes Bangladesh, and the Belt and Road Initiative’s Space Information Corridor . There is no question that Indian spaceflight is technologically superior to that of Pakistan, but the Shenzhou-24 mission is a reminder that China’s technological superiority vis-à-vis India’s leaves India with an unequal contest. India has been ceding the neighbourhood to China’s space networks, and by squandering the opportunities afforded by science diplomacy, it has left Pakistan to look to China even on problems it shares with India. The Apollo-Soyuz interaction during the Cold War and India and Pakistan working together to respond to a locust outbreak barely a year after the Balakot crisis (2019) are testament to the ability of science-based diplomacy to clear room for bilateral engagement with guardrails, without compromising the counter-terrorism agenda. India should revive such engagement.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights. Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: court / Tamil Nadu / religion and belief / history / Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam / democracy / customs and tradition / constitution

1. Core Context & Background: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014. Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An accused wanted in multiple cases in West Bengal’s Asansol, was on Friday (November 27, 2026) shot in his right leg during an alleged clash leading to an exchange of fire with the police when they went to arrest him on Friday morning. The accused, Pratap Das, is wanted in several cases of robbery, theft, iron smuggling, and cyber fraud across Asansol. Police have been searching for him for the past few days in connection with a cyber fraud case lodged last week at Asansol South Police Station. When the police went to arrest him on Friday (November 27, 2026) from a hideout in the Ismail area, he opened fire at the police team. Later, he was shot in retaliatory fire. According to the police, an operation to arrest Pratap was launched on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) when he again opened fire at the police team upon spotting them and managed to flee. The operation was launched by the Asansol Durgapur Police Commissionerate Special Operations Group (SOG), along with officers from Hirapur police station, following a tip-off that he was hiding in the area and carrying a firearm. The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused. Shots of firing were heard in broad daylight causing panic among residents who witnessed a cat and mouse chase between the accused and police. The accused was seen being dragged from one of the houses out by the police with blood dripping from his right leg and was carried on all fours to a police vehicle. Local residents in the area said that they had no idea about the accused. “We did not know that he was hiding in our neighbourhood. I went to drop my daughter off at school when I saw police chasing him. It was scary,” said a woman who stays in the area from where Pratap was arrested. Association for Protection of Democratic Reforms, a civil rights group raised questions about the manner in which police paraded in groups with weapons. “Instead of relying on intelligence inputs, a scientific approach, and proper procedures to apprehend the criminal, the police’s actual objective was to intimidate the general public through a display of firepower,” APDR vice president Ranajit Sur said. The development comes after a total of five encounters that took place in West Bengal since the new Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Five people who have been shot dead by the police during these incidents include three accused in rape cases of minors and two accused of murder.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: police / shooting (crime) / Bharatiya Janata Party

1. Core Context & Background: ‘The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route,’ said Omar Abdullah

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday (November 27, 2026) said not a single foot of blacktopping was carried out on the Amarnath route, while referring to the Sheshnag controversy, and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of “deliberately pitting Hindus and Muslims against each other”. “The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot [referring to the PDP] are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route. They are alleging macadamisation. I challenge them to prove a single foot of blacktopping done on the route. I am ready to face an inquiry. There is a court [Supreme Court] direction to have a 12-feet stretch,” said Mr. Abdullah. Mr. Abdullah’s statement came days after local parties, religious leaders, environmentalists and civil society bodies reacted sharply to the presence of an earthmover close functioning to the Sheshnag lake situation at an altitude of 11,780 feet on the way to the Amarnath shrine, which is around 20 km away from the spot. A report prepared by the J&K Forest Department on the viral video, in which an earthmover was seen close to the lake, said, “The activity seen in the video is part of routine annual maintenance operations being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation [BRO]. No new road construction or fresh alignment is being undertaken. It is further clarified that the Yatra track runs along the right-hand side of the lake and is situated at a considerable distance from the lake. “It said the lake remains protected and the maintenance activity in question “was not intended to alter its character or ecological integrity”. “The matter may, therefore, be viewed in its proper context, keeping in view the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the safety requirements of the annual pilgrimage and the longstanding nature of the track maintenance operations,” it added, while underlining that the maintenance and improvement of this track is a longstanding exercise undertaken regularly since 2012 and “not a new activity initiated in 2026”. However, Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, who was denied permission to visit the spot with police citing security concerns, has asked the government to allow a team of politicians and experts to visit the Sheshnag lake. “If the Union Territory [UT] government is relying on satellite images to claim that no construction is taking place at Sheshnag, why not allow us to visit the site and see for ourselves? The JCBs wreaking havoc there are visible for all to see. To dispel all doubts, let the Chief Minister depute a team of political leaders and environmentalists to inspect the site and establish the truth. What is there to hide?” said Ms. Mufti. Meanwhile, referring to the allegations of irregularities in the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted by the J&K Service Selection Board JKSSB), Mr. Abdullah said, “Political opponents were exploiting the concerns of unemployed youth and creating unnecessary mistrust about the recruitment process. I am always ready to admit if a mistake is committed. But when I dug deep into the matter, I found that instead of there being fraud in the examination, the fact is that the system worked properly. The paper did not leak. The paper was not stolen.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Terming the incident as a case of “attempted cheating but disallowed”, Mr. Abdullah said, “There were people who tried to cheat in the examination. I agree with this. They took out the question paper from the examination hall, used wireless devices and tried to get answers. But they were caught on the spot. They were arrested. The JKSSB should have been praised for it,” said Mr. Abdullah.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The TVK MLA was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A case was registered after the Madras High Court recently directed the State Public Prosecutor to get in touch with the officer regarding the allegations after she filed a formal police complaint . Police sources said a team led by Shristi Singh, the Investigating Officer appointed by the Madras High Court , arrested the legislator at his residence in Kallakurichi on Friday evening and took him in a police vehicle. He was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed. The Kallakurichi All Women Police, which had registered a sexual harassment case against the MLA, served summons on Mr. Vignesh on Wednesday directing him to appear for questioning in connection with the case. Speculation over his arrest grew after Inspector Bhuvaneshwari, attached to the All Women Police station, visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi on Wednesday (November 25) and handed the summons to him in person . On 23.11.2026, a senior lady officer in Kallakurichi District preferred complaint against Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency regarding alleged harassment and inappropriate conduct. On the same day, a case in Kallakurichi AWPS Cr No. 91/2026 was registered under appropriate sections of law. Initial investigation was done by the local police and on the directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in WP (Crl) No. 3183/2026 dated 24.11.2026, Tmt. Shristi Singh, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Tiruppur District took investigation of this case under the supervision of Tmt. N. Kamini, IPS, Inspector General of Police, Administration, Chennai. During the investigation, the petitioner and other witnesses have been enquired by the Investigation Officer. Consequent to the enquiry, the alleged accused Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency has been arrested and the investigation is under progress. Relating to this incident, 201 social media posts were pulled down by the local police and the Cyber Crime Department of Tamil Nadu Police. However, since the Hon'ble High Court has also ordered against publishing, communicating or making known to the public any of the matters covered under sections PoSH Act, it is requested to avoid posting any post in contravention to the above directions.. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Ms. Singh began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini also visited Kallakurichi on Thursday (November 26) and supervised the investigation.
